Therefore by these they were rightly punished, And tortured by a multitude of beasts.
Instead of this punishment, dealing favourably with Your own people, You prepared for them delicacies for food, Even quails to arouse their appetite;

So that they, desiring food, Due to the ugly sight of the beasts sent among them, Might loathe even that which they desired. But these, suffering hardship for a short time, Might be made partakers of delicacies.
For it was necessary, that upon those oppressors suffering should come, which they could not avoid. But to these it should only be shown how their enemies were punished.
For when the fearful fierceness of beasts came upon them, And they perished with the stings of writhing serpents, Your wrath did not endure forever.
But they were troubled for a little while that they might be warned, Receiving a sign of deliverance, to remind them of the Command of Your Law.
For he who turned himself toward it was not saved by that which he saw, But by You, who are the Saviour of all.
And in this You made Your enemies confess, That it is You who delivers from all evil.
For the biting of locusts and flies killed them, Neither was there found any healing for their life: For they deserved to be punished by such.
But Your sons were not overcome by the very fangs of venomous serpents, For Your kindness was continually upon them, and healed them.
For they were pierced, that they should remember Your Words, And were quickly delivered, So not to fall into deep forgetfulness, That they remember Your goodness.
For it was neither herb, nor poultice, that healed them, But Your Word, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, that heals all.
For You have power of life and death. You lead to the gates of She’ol, and bring up again.
Because of his evil a man kills, And the spirit, when it is gone, does not return; Neither the being that is taken up comes again.
But it is impossible to escape Your hand.
For the wicked, that denied to know You, Were beaten by the strength of Your arm; They were pursued with strange rains, hail and showers that they could not avoid, And they were consumed by fire.
For the fire - which is most astounding - had more force in the water, that quenches all; For the world fights for the righteous.
For at one time the flame was restrained, That it might not consume the beasts that were sent against the wicked; But seeing this they might see that they were punished with the judgment of Elohim.
And at another time it burns stronger than fire even in the midst of water, That it might destroy the increase of an unrighteous land.
Instead You fed Your own people with food of messengers, And sent them bread from the shamayim prepared without their labour, Able to content every delight, and pleasant to every taste.
For your sustenance revealed Your sweetness toward Your children, And serving to the appetite of the eater, Rendered itself to every man’s liking.
But snow and ice endured the fire, without melting, That they might know that fire burning in the hail, and flashing in the rain, Destroyed the increase of their enemies.
But this again forgot even its own strength, That the righteous might be nourished.
For the creation that serves You, the Maker, Increases its strength against the unrighteous for their punishment. And diminishes its strength for the benefit of those who put their trust in You.
Therefore even then was it changed into all forms. And was obedient to Your favour, who sustains all, According to the desire of those who had need;
That Your children, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, whom You love, might know, That it is not the growing of crops that nourishes man; But that it is Your Word, that preserves those who put their trust in You.
For that which was not destroyed by the fire, Being warmed with a few rays of sun, soon melted away,
That it might be known that we must rise before the sun and give You thanks, And pray to you at the daybreak.
For the expectancy of the unthankful shall melt away as the winter frost, And shall run away as useless water.
For Your judgments are great, and cannot be expressed; Therefore beings not instructed have strayed.

For when unrighteous men thought to oppress the qodesh nation; They, being shut up in their houses, the prisoners of darkness, And shackled in the bonds of a long night, Lay exiled from the anticipation of eternity.
For while they thought to lie hidden in their secret sins, They were scattered under a dark veil of forgetfulness, Being greatly astonished, and troubled with visions.
For neither could the corner that held them keep them from fear: But noises falling down sounded about them, And mournful visions appeared to them with a heavy presence.
No power of the fire could give them light: Nor could the bright flames of the stars endure to lighten that horrible night.
Only a very dreadful fire kindled by itself appeared to them; For being greatly afraid, they thought that which they saw to be worse than the sight they did not see.
As for the illusions of magic, they were brought to naught, And their boasting in wisdom was reproved with shame.
For those who promised to drive away fear and troubles from a sick being, Were sick themselves of fear, worthy to be laughed at.
For though no fearsome matter frightened them; Yet being scared of beasts that passed by, and hissing of serpents,
They perished from fear, Denying that they saw the air, which could in no way be avoided.
For wickedness, condemned by her own witness, Is very fearful, and being pressured by conscience, always foresees difficulties.
For fear is naught but a betrayal of the support which reason offers.
And the expectation from within, being lesser, Counts the ignorance greater than the cause which brings the torment.
But they sleeping the same sleep that night, which was indeed unbearable, And which came upon them out of the imminent depths of She’ol,
Were on one hand tortured with fearsome visions, And on the other hand fainted, their heart failing them; For a sudden unexpected fear came upon them.
So then whoever fell down there was thus kept, shut up in a prison without iron bars,
For whether he were a farmer, or shepherd, Or a labourer in the field, He was overtaken, and endured that unavoidable necessity; For they were all bound with one chain of darkness.
Whether it wore a whistling wind, Or a melodious noise of birds among the spreading branches. Or a pleasant waterfall running forcefully.

Or a terrible sound of stones thrown down, Or a stampeding of beasts that could not be seen, Or a roaring voice of most savage wild beasts, Or a rebounding echo from the hollow mountains; These made them to faint for fear.
For the whole world shone with radiant light, And none were hindered in their labour;
Over them alone was spread a heavy night, An image of that darkness which would afterward receive them; But they were even more grievous unto themselves than the darkness.
Nevertheless, your qodeshim had a very great light, Whose voice they heard, but did not see their shape, They also counted them baruḵ, for they had not likewise suffered.
And because of this, they did not harm those by whom they had been wronged before, they thanked them, And pleaded for their forgiveness that they had been enemies.
Instead of this You gave them a burning pillar of fire, Both to be a guide for the unknown journey, And a harmless sun to comfort them in esteem.
For they deserved to be deprived of light and imprisoned in darkness, Who had kept Your sons imprisoned, By whom the incorruptible light of the Law was to be given unto the world.

And when they had determined to slay the infants of the qodeshim, One child being thrown forth, but saved, To reprove them, You took away the multitude of their children, And destroyed them altogether in a mighty flood.
Of that night our fathers were informed before, That knowing with certainty unto what promises they had trusted, They might afterwards be of good courage.
So both the salvation of the righteous, And destruction of their enemies was accepted by Your people.
For by which You punished our adversaries, By the same You esteemed us, whom You had called.

For the righteous children of good men made offerings secretly, And with one accord made a qodesh law, That the qodeshim should likewise be partakers of the same good and evil, The fathers now singing out the songs of praise.
But on the other side was the sound of a despairing cry of the enemies, And a grievous noise was spread abroad for children that were bewailed.
The master and the servant were punished after one manner; And the sovereign suffered the same as the common person.
So altogether they had innumerable dead with one kind of death; Nor were the living sufficient to bury them; For in one moment the most noble of their offspring was destroyed.
For although they would not believe by reason of their magic; Upon the destruction of the firstborn, they acknowledged these people to be the sons of Elohim.
For while all was in quiet silence, And that night was in the midst of its swift course,
Your mighty Word leaped out of the shamayim from Your royal throne, As a fierce man of battle into the midst of a land of destruction,
And brought Your sincere Command as a sharp sword, And stood filling all with death; And it touched the shamayim, but stood upon the earth.
Then suddenly visions of horrible dreams troubled them greatly. And fears not sought for came upon them.
And one thrown here, and another there half dead, Revealed the cause of his death.
For the dreams that troubled them forewarned this, Lest they should perish, and not know why they were afflicted.
Indeed, the taste of death touched the righteous also, And there was a destruction of the multitude in the wilderness; But the wrath did not endure long.

For then a blameless man hurried, And stood forth to defend them; And bringing the shield of his own service, Even prayer, and the atonement of incense, Opposed the wrath, and brought the calamity to an end, Declaring that he was Your servant.
So he overcame the destroyer, not with strength of body, Nor with force of arms, But with a word subdued He who punished, Declaring the oaths and Covenants made with the fathers.
For when the dead had fallen down in heaps one upon another, Standing between, he held back the wrath, And parted the way to the living.
For in the long garment was the whole world, And in the four rows of the stones was engraved the esteem of the fathers, And Your excellence upon the turban of his head.
To these the destroyer yielded, and feared; For it was enough that they only tasted the wrath.
As for the wicked, wrath came upon them without kindness to their end; For He knew before what they would do;
How having allowed them to depart, and sent them away in haste, They would reconsider and pursue them.
For while they were still mourning and lamenting at the graves of the dead, They added another foolish scheme, and pursued as fugitives, Those whom they had begged to leave.

For the expectancy of which they were worthy, drew them toward this end, And made them forget that which had already come to be, That they might fill the punishment of their torment which was lacking;
And that Your people might travel an extraordinary way, But they would find a strange death.
For the whole creation in its kind was renewed in fashion, Serving Your Commands that were given to them, That Your children might be guarded without harm;
As a cloud overshadowing the camp. And where water stood before, dry land appeared, And out of the Sea of Reeds, an unobstructed way; And out of the raging river, a green field,
Where all the people went through that were defended by Your hand, Seeing Your marvelous, awesome wonders.
For they reared like horses, and leaped like lambs, Praising you, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, who had delivered them.
For they still remembered what was done while they sojourned in the strange land, How the ground brought forth flies instead of cattle, And how the river threw up multitudes of frogs instead of fish.
But afterwards they saw a new offspring of birds, When being led with their appetite, they asked for luxurious meats.
For quails came up to them from the sea for their satisfaction.

And punishments came upon the sinners, Not without former signs of the power of thunder; For they suffered rightly according to their own wickedness, Because they exercised a harder and hateful behaviour toward sojourners.
For the Seḏomites did not receive those who were unknown when they came, But these brought friends into slavery, that deserved good from them.
And not only so, but supposed some respect would be had of those, Because they treated sojourners hatefully.
But they afflicted those grievously, whom they had received with feasting, And had already shared in the same laws with them.
Therefore they were stricken with blindness, As those at the doors of the righteous man; When being surrounded with great, horrible darkness, Every one sought to pass by his own doors.

For the elements were changed in themselves by a kind of harmony, As notes change the name of the tune on a harp And yet are always sounds; Which are understood by the sight of that which has been done.
For those of the earth were turned into watery, And that which before swam in the water, now moved on the earth.
The fire had power in the water, forgetting its own ability; And the water forgot its own quenching nature.
On the contrary, the flames did not destroy the flesh of the corruptible living matters, though they walked in them; Neither melted the frosty food from the shamayim that would naturally melt.
For in all matters O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, You exalted Your people and esteemed them, Neither did You lightly regard them, But assisted them at every time and place.

The Prologue: Whereas many and great matters have been delivered to us through the Torah and the neḇi’im and by others that have followed their paths, for which Yisra’ĕl ought to be commended for learning and wisdom; and of which not only the readers need to become competent themselves, but also those who desire to learn be able to benefit those who are outside, both by speaking and writing. My grandfather Yahoshua, when he had applied himself greatly to the reading of the Law, and the neḇi’im, and other Books of our fathers, and had acquired good judgment from them, was himself also led to write somewhat pertaining to learning and wisdom; to the intent that those who desire to learn, and are drawn to such, might profit much more in living according to the Law. Therefore let me plead that you read it with good intent and attention, and to pardon us for where we may seem to come short in some words, which we have laboured to interpret. For the same words spoken in Iḇri, and translated into another tongue, do not have the same force in them; and not only this, but the Law itself, and the neḇi’im, and the rest of the Books, have great difference, when they are spoken in their own language. For in the thirty-eighth year of coming into Mitsrayim, when Euergetĕs was sovereign, and continuing there some time, I found a book of great learning; therefore I thought it necessary for me to devote some diligence and labour to interpret it; using great vigilance and skill in that time to complete the book, and also publish it for those in a foreign land who are willing to learn, being prepared before in manners to live after the Law.
All wisdom comes from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and is with Him forever.
Who may number the sand of the sea and the drops of rain, And the days of eternity?
Who may search out the height of the shamayim, And the breadth of the earth, and the deep, and wisdom?
Wisdom has been created before all, And the understanding of insight from everlasting.
The Word of Elohim Most High is the fountain of wisdom; And her ways are everlasting Commands.
To whom has the root of wisdom been revealed? Or who has known her wise counsels?
Unto whom has the knowledge of wisdom been made manifest? And who has understood her great experience?
There is One wise and greatly to be revered: 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 sitting upon His throne.
He created her, and saw her, and measured her, And poured her out upon all His works.
She is with all flesh according to His gift, And He has given her to those who love Him.
The reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is esteem and splendour and gladness, And a crown of rejoicing.
The reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 makes a glad heart, And gives joy, and gladness, and a long life.
It shall go well to the end for he who reveres 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, And he shall find favour in the day of his death.
To revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is the beginning of wisdom: And it was created with the trustworthy in the womb.
She has built an everlasting foundation with men, And she shall continue with their seed.
To revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is fullness of wisdom, And fills men with her fruits.
She fills all their house with that which is desirable, And the gatherers with her increase.
The reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is a crown of wisdom, Making peace and perfect health to flourish; Both of which are gifts of Elohim; And it increases the rejoicing of those that love Him.
Wisdom rains down skill and knowledge of understanding, And exalts to esteem those who hold her fast.
The root of wisdom is to revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, And the branches thereof are long life.
The reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 drives away sins, And where it is present, it turns away wrath.
A wrathful man cannot be declared right; For the sway of his wrath shall be his destruction.
A patient man shall weep for a time, And afterward joy shall spring up in him.
He shall hold his words for a time, And the lips of many shall declare his wisdom.
The parables of knowledge are in the treasures of wisdom: But reverence is an abomination to a sinner.
If you desire wisdom, guard the Commands, And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall give her to you.
For the reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is wisdom and instruction; And belief and meekness are his delight.
Do not doubt the reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 when you are poor: And do not come to him with a double mind.
Do not be a hypocrite in the sight of men, And take heed what you speak.

Do not exalt yourself, lest you fall, and bring shame upon yourself, And so Elohim uncover your secrets, and throw you down in the midst of the assembly, Because you did not come in truth to the reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, But your heart is full of deceit.
My son, if you come to serve 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, Prepare your being for trial.
Prepare your heart, and constantly endure, And do not hasten in time of trouble.
Cling to Him, and do not depart, That you may be increased at your latter end.
Whatsoever is brought upon you, accept cheerfully, And be patient when you are brought low.
For gold is tried in the fire, And acceptable men in the furnace of adversity.
Believe in Him, and He shall help you; Establish your way, and trust in Him.
You who revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, wait for His kindness; And do not turn aside, lest you fall.
You who revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, believe Him; And your reward shall not fail.
You who revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, have expectancy for good, And for everlasting joy and kindness.
Look at the generations of old and see; Did any ever trust in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and were put to shame? Or did any remain in His reverence, and were forsaken? Or whom did He ever despise, that called upon Him?
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is full of compassion and kindness, Patient, and very tender-hearted, and forgives sins, And saves in time of affliction.
Woe unto fearful hearts, and faint hands, And the sinner that goes two ways!
Woe unto he who is fainthearted! For he is unbelieving; Therefore he shall not be defended.
Woe unto you that have lost patience! And what shall you do when 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall punish you?
Those who 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall not disobey His Word; And those who love Him guard His Ways.
Those who revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 seek that which is well- pleasing to Him; And those who love Him shall be filled with the Torah.
Those who revere prepare 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 their hearts, And humble their beings in His sight,
Saying, “We shall fall into the hands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and not into the hands of men; For as His excellence is, so is His kindness.”
Hear me your father, O children, and do accordingly, that you may be safe.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has given the father esteem over the children, And has confirmed the authority of the mother over the sons.
Whoever esteems his father makes an atonement for his sins;
And he who esteems his mother is as one who stores up treasure.
Whoever esteems his father shall have joy from his own children; And when he makes his prayer, he shall be heard.
He who esteems his father shall have a long life; And he who is obedient to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall be a comfort to his mother.
He who reveres 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall esteem his father, And shall do service unto his parents, as to his masters.
Esteem your father and mother both in word and deed, That a beraḵah may come upon you from them.
For the beraḵah of the father establishes the houses of children; But the curse of the mother roots out foundations.
Do not rejoice in the shame of your father; For your father’s shame is no esteem unto you.
For the esteem of a man is from the esteem of his father; And a mother in shame is a reproach to the children.
My son, help your father in his age, And do not grieve him as long as he lives.
And if his understanding fails, have patience with him; And do not despise him when you are in your full strength.
For the relief for your father shall not be forgotten; And instead of sin, it shall be added to build you up.
In the day of your affliction it shall be remembered; Your sins also shall melt away, as the ice in the fair warm weather.
He who forsakes his father is as a blasphemer; And he who displeases his mother is cursed of Elohim.
My son, go on with your business in meekness; So you shall be beloved of He who approves.
The greater you are, the more you humble yourself, And you shall find favour before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
Many are in high places, and of name; But mysteries are revealed to the meek.
For the power of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is great, And He is esteemed by the lowly.
Do not search out that which is too hard for you, Neither seek that which is above your strength.
But what is Commanded, think upon this with reverence, For it is not necessary for you to see with your eyes that which is secret.
Do not be curious in unnecessary matters: For more is revealed to you than men understand.
For many are deceived by their own worthless opinion; And evil suspicion has overthrown their judgment.
Without eyes there is no light; Do not profess the knowledge which you do not have.
A stubborn heart shall suffer evil in the end; And he who loves danger shall perish in it.
A hard heart shall be loaded with sorrows; And the wicked man shall heap sin upon sin.
In the punishment of the proud there is no remedy; For the plant of wickedness has taken root in him.
The heart of the clever shall understand a parable; And an attentive ear is the desire of a wise man.
Water shall quench a flaming fire; And kind deeds make an atonement for sins.
And he who repays good deeds remembers that which may come after; And when he falls, he shall find a support.
My son, do not rob the poor of his living, And do not allow the needy eyes to wait long.
Do not make a hungry being sorrowful; Neither provoke a man in his distress.
Do not add more trouble to a heart that is tortured; And do not delay to give to he who is in need.
Do not reject the supplication of the afflicted; Neither turn away your face from a poor man.
Do not turn away your eye from the needy, And give him no occasion to curse you;
For if he curses you in the bitterness of his being, His prayer shall be heard by He who made him.
Earn for yourself the love of the assembly, And bow your head to a great man.
Let it not grieve you to bend your ear to the poor, And give him a friendly answer with meekness.
Deliver he who suffers wrong from the hand of the oppressor; And do not be faint-hearted when you sit in judgment.
Be as a father to the fatherless, And like a husband to their mother; So you shall be as the Ben of the Most High, And He shall love you more than your mother does.
Wisdom exalts her children, And lays hold of those who seek her.
He who loves her loves ḥai; And those who seek her early shall be filled with joy.
He who holds her fast shall inherit esteem; And wherever she enters, 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall baraḵ.
Those who serve her serve the Qadosh One: And those who love her 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 loves.
Whoever gives ear to her shall judge the nations: And he who attends to her shall dwell securely.
If a man commits himself to her, he shall inherit her; And his generation shall hold her in possession.
For at first she shall walk by him in crooked ways, And bring fear and dread upon him, And punish him with her discipline, Until she may trust his being, and try him by her laws.
Then she shall return him to the straight way, And comfort him, and show him her secrets.
But if he goes wrong, she shall forsake him, And give him over to his own ruin.
Watch for opportunity, and beware of evil; And do not be ashamed when it concerns your being.
For there is shame that brings sin; And there is shame which is esteem and favour.
Do not show partiality against your being, And do not let the fear of any man cause you to fall.
And do not refrain to speak, when there is occasion to do good, And do not hide your wisdom in her loveliness.
For by speech wisdom shall be known; And learning by the word of the tongue.
By no means speak against the truth; But be ashamed of the straying of your ignorance.
Do not be ashamed to confess your sins; And do not force the course of the river.
Do not make yourself a servant to a foolish man; Neither show partiality to the mighty.
Strive for the truth unto death, And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall fight for you.
Do not be hasty with your tongue, Or slack and negligent in your deeds.
Do not be as a lion in your house, Nor wroth among your servants.
Do not let your hand be stretched out to receive, And closed when you should repay.
Do not lay your heart upon your goods; And do not say, “I have enough for my life.”
Do not follow your own mind and strength, To walk in the ways of your heart:
And do not say, “Who shall control me in my deeds?” For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall surely punish your pride.
Do not say, “I have sinned, and what harm has befallen me? For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is patient, He shall by no means let you go.
Concerning atonement, Do not be without reverence to add sin unto sin;
And do not say, “His kindness is great; He shall be appeased for the multitude of my sins.” For kindness and wrath come from Him, And His wrath rests upon sinners.
Do not delay to turn to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and do not put off from day to day; For suddenly the wrath of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall come forth, And in your security you shall be destroyed, And perish in the day of vengeance.
Do not lay your heart upon goods acquired unrighteously, For they shall not profit you in the day of calamity.
Do not winnow with every wind, and do not go into every way: For so does the sinner that has a double tongue.
Be steadfast in your understanding; And let your word be the same.
Be swift to hear; and let your being be sincere; And give answer with patience.
If you have understanding, answer your neighbour; If not, put your hand over your mouth.
Esteem and shame is in speech; And the tongue of man is his downfall.
Do not be a whisperer, and do not lie in wait with your tongue; For foul shame is upon the thief, and an evil condemnation upon the double- tongued.
Do not be ignorant of any matter, great or a small.
Do not become an enemy instead of a friend; For you shall inherit an evil name, shame, and reproach; Even as a sinner that has a double tongue.
Do not exalt yourself in the counsel of your own heart; That your being be not torn in pieces as a bull.
You shall consume your leaves, and lose your fruit, And leave yourself as a dry tree.
A wicked being shall destroy he who possesses, And shall cause him to be laughed to scorn by his enemies.
Sweet words shall multiply friends, And a favourable tongue shall increase kind greetings.
Be at peace with many; But have just one counsellor in a thousand.
If you would get a friend, prove him first and do not be hasty to trust him.
For a certain man is a friend for his own occasion, And shall not remain in the day of your trouble.
And there is a friend, who being turned to enmity, shall cause strife and uncover your reproach.
Again, there is a friend, a companion at the table, But shall not continue in the day of your affliction.
When you are prosperous he shall be as you are, And shall be bold over your servants.
If you are brought low, he shall be against you, And shall hide himself from your face.
Separate yourself from your enemies, And be on guard with your friends.
A trustworthy friend is a strong defence; And he who has found such a one has found a treasure.
There is none that makes up for a trustworthy friend, And his worth is invaluable.
A trustworthy friend is the healing of life; And those who revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall find Him.
Whoever reveres 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 directs his friendship well; For as he is, so shall his neighbour be also.
My son, gather instruction from your youth onward; So you shall gain wisdom till your old age.
Come to her as one that plows and sows, and wait for her good fruit; For you shall not toil much in labouring over her, But you shall eat of her fruit soon enough.
She is very unpleasant to the unlearned; He who is without understanding shall not remain with her.
She shall lay upon him as a mighty stone of trial; And he shall throw her from him before long.
For wisdom is according to her name, And she is not revealed to many.
Listen my son, receive my advice, And do not refuse my counsel,
And put your feet into her shackles, And your neck into her chain.
Bow down your shoulder, and bear her, And do not be grieved with her bonds.
Come to her with your whole heart, And guard her ways with all your strength.
Search and seek, and she shall be made known unto you; And when you have taken hold of her, do not let her go.
For in the end you shall find her rest, And that shall turn out for your joy.
Then her shackles shall be a strong defence for you, And her chains a robe of esteem.
For there is a golden ornament upon her, And her bands are purple lace.
You shall put her on as a robe of esteem, And shall lay her upon you as a crown of joy.
My son, if you allow, you shall be taught; And if you apply your mind, you shall be clever.
If you love to listen, you shall receive understanding; And if you bow your ear, you shall be wise,
Stand in the group of the elders; And cling to he who is wise.
Be willing to hear every worthy discourse; And do not let the parables of understanding escape you.
And if you see a man of understanding, Get yourself to him early, And let your feet wear out his doorstep.
Let your mind be upon the Laws of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, And consider His Commands continually; He shall establish your heart, and give you the wisdom you desire.
Do no evil, so no harm shall come to you.
Depart from the unrighteous, and evil shall turn away from you.
My son, do not sow upon the furrows of unrighteousness, And you shall not reap them sevenfold.
Do not seek superiority from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, Neither of the royal seat of esteem.
Do not declare yourself right before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄; And do not boast of your wisdom before the sovereign.
Do not seek to be judge, being unable to remove evil; Lest at any time you be partial to the mighty, A stumbling block in the way of your uprightness.
Do not cause the crowd of a city to stumble, And then you shall not be brought low among the people.
Do not bind one sin upon another; For not one shall go unpunished.
Do not say, “Elohim shall look upon the multitude of my offerings, And when I offer to the Most High Elohim, He shall accept it.”
Do not be faint-hearted when you make your prayer, And do not neglect to give in kindness.
Mock no man in the bitterness of his being; For there is One who humbles and exalts.
Do not plan a lie against your brother; Neither do likewise to your friend.
Refuse to make any manner of lie; For the way of this is not good.
Do not use many words among a multitude of elders, And do not make much babbling when you pray.
Do not hate laborious work, neither work of the land, Which the Most High has ordained.
Do not number yourself among the crowd of sinners, But remember that wrath shall not delay.
Humble yourself greatly; For the punishment of the wicked is fire and worms.
Do not exchange a friend for goods by any means; Neither a trustworthy brother for the gold of Ophir.
Do not forsake a wise and good woman; For her favour is above gold.
When your servant works trustworthily, do not mistreat him. Nor the hired man that gives himself completely for you.
Let your being love a good servant, and do not withhold his freedom.
Do you have cattle? Keep an eye on them; And if they are for your profit, keep them with you.
Do you have children? Instruct them, And bow their neck from their youth.
Do you have daughters? Look after their body, And do not be too generous toward them.
Give your daughter in marriage, and you shall have performed a weighty matter; But give her to a man of understanding.
Do you have a wife in mind? Do not forsake her; And do not give yourself over to an easy woman.
Esteem your father with your whole heart, And do not forget the sorrows of your mother.
Remember that you were brought forth by them; And how would you repay them what they have done for you?
Revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with all your being, and revere His kohenim.
Love He who made you with all your strength, And do not forsake his servants.

Revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and honour the kohĕn; And give him his portion, as it is Commanded you; The first-fruits, and the guilt offering, and the wave offering, And the qodesh offering, and the first-fruits of qodeshah.
And stretch out your hand to the poor, That your beraḵah may be perfected.
A gift has favour in the sight of every living man; And do not hold back for the dead.
Do not fail to accompany those who weep, And mourn with those who mourn.
Do not be slow to visit the sick; For that shall cause you to be loved.
Whatever you take in hand, remember the end, And you shall never do wrong.
Do not strive with a mighty man lest you fall into his hands.
Do not quarrel with a wealthy man, lest he outweigh you; For gold has destroyed many, and twisted the hearts of sovereigns.
Do not strive with a man that is a babbler, And do not heap wood upon his fire.
Do not jest with a rude man, Lest your ancestors be shamed.
Do not reproach a man that turns from sin, But remember that we are all worthy of punishment.
Do not shame a man in his old age; For even some of us grow old.
Do not rejoice over the death of your greatest enemy, But remember that we all die.
Do not despise the discourse of the wise, But acquaint yourself with their proverbs; For from them you shall learn instruction, And how to serve great men with ease.
Do not avoid the discourse of the elders; For they also learned from their fathers, And from them you shall learn understanding, And to give answer as needed.
Do not kindle the coals of a sinner, Lest you be burned with the flame of his fire.
Do not rise up at the presence of an insuiter, Lest he lie in wait to entrap you in your words.
Do not lend to he who is mightier than yourself; For if you lend to him, count it but lost.
Do not be guarantor above your ability; For if you be guarantor, take care to pay it.
Do not go to law against a judge; For they shall judge for him according to his esteem.
Do not travel on the way with one who is headstrong, Lest he become burdensome to you; For he shall do according to his own desire, And you shall perish with him through his folly.
Do not strive with a man of wrath, And do not go with him to a lonely place; For bloodshed is naught in his sight, And where there is no help, he shall overthrow you.
Do not counsel a fool; For he does not heed advice.
Do not speak secrets before a stranger; For you do not know what he shall reveal.
Do not open your heart to every man, Lest he repay you craftily.
Do not be jealous over the wife of your bosom, And do not teach her an evil lesson against yourself.
Do not give yourself to a woman to trample your strength.
Do not go into a whore, lest you fall into her snares.
Do not keep company with a flirtatious woman, Lest you be taken by her attempts.
Do not stare upon a maiden, So you do not fall by that which is precious in her.
Do not give yourself to whores, So that you do not lose your inheritance.
Do not look about in the streets of the city, Neither wander in its lonely places.
Turn your eye away from a good- looking woman, And do not look upon another’s loveliness; For many have been deceived by the loveliness of a woman; For desire is kindled by it like a fire.

Do not sit at all with another man’s wife, Nor sit down with her in your arms, And do not spend your silver with her on wine; Lest your heart incline toward her, And so, through your desire fall into destruction.
Do not forsake an old friend; For the new is not comparable to him. A new friend is like new wine; When it is old, you shall drink it with pleasure.
Do not envy the esteem of a sinner; For you do not know what his end shall be.
Do not delight in that which the wicked have pleasure in; But remember they shall not go unpunished to their grave.

Keep far from the man who has power to kill; So the fear of death shall not concern you. And if you encounter him, make no mistake, Lest he take away your life immediately. Remember that you walk in the midst of snares, And that you walk upon the walls of the city.
When you draw near, reason with your neighbour, And consult with the wise.
Let your words be with the wise, And all your talk in the Law of the Most High.
And let righteous men eat and drink with you; And let your esteem be in the reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
For the hand of the craftsman the work shall be praised, And the wise ruler of the people for his words.
A man of an evil tongue is dangerous in his city; And he who is hasty with his words shall be hated.
A wise judge shall instruct his people; And the reign of a clever man is well ordered.
As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers; And what manner of man the ruler of the city is, Such are all those who dwell in it.
An unwise sovereign destroys his people; But through the insight of those who are in authority the city shall be inhabited.
The power of the earth is in the hand 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, And in due time He shall appoint it to One who is worthy.
The prosperity of man is in the hand of Elohim; And He shall lay His esteem upon the face of the scribe.
Do not bear hatred against your neighbour for every wrong; And do not act as an insulter at all.
Pride is hateful before Elohim and man; And against both, one commits wickedness.
Because of unrighteous dealings, maltreatment, and wealth gained by deceit, The rule is transferred from one people to another.
How could earth and ashes be proud? There is none more wicked than a covetous man; For such a one puts his own being up for sale; For while he lives he destroys his inner being.
The physician ends a long disease; And he who is a sovereign today shall die tomorrow.
For when a man is dead, He shall inherit insects, creatures and worms.
The beginning of pride is when one departs from Elohim, And his heart is turned away from his Maker.
For pride is the beginning of sin, And he who has it shall pour out abominations: And therefore 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 brings upon them unknown calamity, And overthrows them completely.
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has thrown down the thrones of proud princes, And appointed the meek in their place.
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has plucked up the roots of the proud nations, And planted the lowly in their place.
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 overthrew the lands of the gentiles, And destroyed them to the foundations of the earth.
He took some of them away, and destroyed them, And has caused their remembrance to cease from the earth.
Pride was not made for man, Nor violent wrath for those who are born of a woman.
Those who revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 are a continual seed, And those who love Him an esteemed plant. Those who disregard the Law are a shameful seed; Those who transgress the Commands are a deceptive seed.
Among brothers he who is chief is esteemed; So are those who revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in His eyes.
The reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 goes before the obtaining of authority; But stubbornness and pride is the loss of it.
Whether he is wealthy, noble or poor, Their esteem is the reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
It is not right to despise the poor who has understanding; Neither is it proper to exalt a sinner.
Great men and judges and rulers shall be esteemed; Yet there is none greater than he who reveres 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
Those who are free shall do service to the servant that is wise; And he who has knowledge shall not grumble when he is instructed.
Do not be overwise in doing your business; And do not boast in the time of your distress.
Better is he who labours and overflows in all, Than he who boasts and lacks bread.
My son, esteem your being in meekness, And give it respect according to its quality.
Who shall declare right he who sins against his own being? And who shall esteem he who shames his own life?
The poor man is esteemed for his skill, And the wealthy man is esteemed for his wealth.
He who is esteemed in poverty, how much more in wealth? And he who is ashamed in wealth, how much more in poverty?
Wisdom lifts up the head of he who is of low degree, And makes him to sit among great men.
Do not commend a man for his good looks; Neither despise a man for his outward appearance.
The bee is little among those that fly; But her fruit is the first of that which is sweet.
Do not boast of your garments and clothes, And do not exalt yourself in the day of esteem; For the works of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 are wondrous, And His works among men are hidden.
Many sovereigns have sat down on the ground; And one that was never considered has worn the crown.
Many mighty men have been greatly shamed; And those esteemed delivered into other men’s hands.
Do not accuse before you have examined the truth; Understand first, and then reprove.
Do not answer before you have heard the case; Neither interrupt men in the middle of speaking.
Do not strive in a matter that does not concern you; And do not sit in judgment with sinners.
My son, do not engage in many matters; For if you strive greatly, you shall not be innocent; And if you pursue, you shall not obtain, Neither shall you escape by fleeing.
There is one who labours, and struggles, and hurries, And is so much more behind.
Again, there is another that is slow, and needs help, Lacking skill, and full of poverty; Yet the eye of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 looks upon him for good, And raises him up from his humiliation,
And lifts his head from misery; So that many see His peace over all this.
Prosperity and adversity, life and death, Poverty and wealth, come from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
Wisdom, knowledge and understanding of the Law, are of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄; Love, and the way of good works, are from Him.
Sin and darkness had their beginning together with sinners; And evil shall grow old with those who boast in them.
The gift of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 remains with the righteous, And His favour brings peace forever.
There is he who grows wealthy by his cunning and frugality, And this is the portion of his reward:
For he says, “I have found rest, and now shall eat continually of my goods.” And yet he does not know what event shall come upon him, And that he must leave those to others, and die.
Be steadfast in your agreement, and be acquainted with it, And grow old in your work.
Do not marvel at the works of sinners; But trust in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and continue in your labour; For it is light in the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to suddenly make a poor man wealthy.
The beraḵah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is in the reward of the reverent, And suddenly He makes his beraḵah flourish.
Do not say, “What profit is there of my service? And what good shall I have afterward?”
Again, do not say, “I have enough, and possess much, And what evil shall come to me afterward?”
In the day of good there is a forgetfulness of affliction; And in the day of affliction there is no remembrance of good.
For it is light for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 to reward a man according to his ways on the day of death.
The affliction of an hour makes a man forget pleasure; And in the end his deeds shall be exposed.
Judge none baruḵ before his death; For a man shall be known in his children.
Do not bring every man into your house; For the deceitful man has many schemes.
As a partridge taken in a cage, So is the heart of the proud; And as a spy, he watches for your fall;
For he lies in wait, and turns good into evil, And in that which is worthy of praise shall accuse you.
From a spark of fire a heap of coals is kindled: And a sinful man lays in wait for blood.
Take heed of an evil-doer, for he works wickedness; Lest he bring upon you an everlasting stain.
Receive a stranger into your house, and he shall disturb you, And turn you out of your own.
When you do good, know to whom you do it; So you shall be thanked for your good works.
Do good to the upright, and you shall find a recompense; And if not from him, even from the Most High.
No good shall come to he who is always occupied with evil, Nor to he who does no kind deed.
Give to the upright man, and do not help a sinner.

Do good to he who is lowly, but do not give to the wicked; Withhold your bread, and do not give it to him, Lest he overthrow you by it; For you shall receive twice as much evil for all the good you have done to him.
For the Most High hates sinners, and shall repay the wicked with retribution, And keeps them for the great day of their punishment.
Give to the good, and do not help the sinner.
A friend cannot be known in good times; And an enemy cannot be hidden in adversity.
In the prosperity of a man enemies shall be grieved: But in his adversity even a friend shall turn away.
Never trust your enemy; For as iron rusts, so is his wickedness.

Though he humbles himself, and comes bowed down, Yet be on your guard and beware of him, And be to him as if you had wiped a mirror, And you shall know that its tarnish has not been wiped away altogether.

Do not put him near you, Lest when he has overthrown you, he stands in your place; Neither let him sit at your right hand, Lest he seek to take your seat, and you remember my words in the end, And be pierced by them.
Who shall pity a charmer that is bitten by a serpent, Or any who come near wild beasts?
So one that goes to a sinner, and is defiled by him in his sins, Who shall pity?
For a while he shall remain with you, But if you begin to fall, he shall not wait.
An enemy speaks sweetly with his lips, But in his heart he imagines how to throw you into a pit; He weeps with his eyes, but if he finds opportunity, He shall not be satisfied with blood.
If adversity comes upon you, you shall find him there first; And though he pretends to help you, even so he shall wrong you.
He shall shake his head, and clap his hands, And whisper much, and change his face.
He who handles tar is made unclean by it; And he who has fellowship with a proud man shall be like him.

Do not burden yourself above your strength while you live; And have no fellowship with one who is mightier and wealthier than yourself; For how is the kettle and the earthen pot in agreement? For if the one be struck against the other, it shall be broken.
The wealthy man has done wrong, and yet he threatens all; The poor is wronged, and he must also plead.
If you profit him, he shall use you; But if you have naught, he shall forsake you.
If you possess whatever, he shall live with you; He shall also leave you naked, and shall not be sorry for it.
If he has need of you, he shall deceive you, And smile at you, and have you in expectancy; He shall speak smooth words to you, and say, “What do you need?”

And he shall shame you with his delicacies, Until he has drained you dry two or three times, And in the end he shall mock you afterward. When he sees you, he shall forsake you, and shake his head at you.
Beware that you are not deceived and brought down in your rejoicing.
If you are invited by a mighty man, withdraw yourself, And he shall invite you so much more.
Do not push yourself on him, lest you be turned away; Do not stand far off, lest you be forgotten.
Do not be eager to be equal to him in speech, And do not believe his many words; For with much talk he shall persuade you, And smiling at you shall draw out your secrets;
But cruelly he shall lay up your words, and not spare to do you harm, And deliver you up.
Observe, and be on your guard, For you walk in danger of being overthrown; When you hear these, awake from your sleep.
Love 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 all your life, And call upon Him for your deliverance.
Every beast loves its kind, And every man loves his neighbour.
All flesh associates according to kind, And a man shall cling to those like himself.
What fellowship has the wolf with the lamb? So the sinner with the righteous.
What agreement is there between the hyena and a dog? And what peace between the wealthy and the poor?
As the wild donkey is the lion’s prey in the wilderness; So the wealthy eat up the poor.
As the proud hate humility; So does the wealthy abhor the poor.
A wealthy man beginning to fall is supported by his friends; But a poor man fallen is pushed away by his friends.

When a wealthy man is fallen, he has many helpers; He speaks words not to be spoken, and yet men declare him right: The poor man slips, and yet they also rebuke him; He speaks wisely, but is not heeded.

When a wealthy man speaks, every man holds his tongue, And look, what he says, they exalt it to the clouds; But if the poor man speaks, they say, “What fellow is this?” And if he stumbles, they shall help to overthrow him.
Wealth is good to he who has no sin, And poverty is evil in the mouth of the wicked.
The heart of a man changes his face, whether it be for good or evil; And a glad heart makes a good face.
A good face is a sign of a heart that is good; And the searching out of parables is a wearisome labour of the mind.
Baruḵ is the man that has not slipped with his mouth, And is not pierced with the great number of sins.
Baruḵ is he whose conscience has not condemned him, And who has not fallen from his expectancy in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
Wealth is not fitting for a miser; And what should an envious man do with silver?
He who gathers by depriving his own being, Gathers for others that shall spend his goods loosely.
He who is evil to himself, to whom shall he be good? He shall not take pleasure in his goods.
There is none worse than he who envies himself; And this is to repay for his wickedness.
And if he does good, he does it unwillingly; And in the end he shall declare his wickedness.
The greedy man has an evil eye; He turns away his face, and despises men.
A covetous man’s eye is not satisfied with his portion; And the wickedness of the wicked dries up his being.
A wicked eye is greedy for bread, And he is a miser at his table.
My son, according to your ability do good to yourself, And give 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 His due offering.
Remember that death shall not be long in coming, And that the promise of the grave is not revealed to you.
Do good to your friend before you die, And according to your ability stretch out your hand and give to him.
Do not deprive yourself of a good day, And do not let the share of a good desire overlook you.
Shall you not leave your hardships to another? And your labours to be divided by lot?
Give and take, and qadosh your being; For there is no seeking delicacies in the grave.
All flesh grows old as a garment; For the promise from the beginning is: You shall die in death.
As the green leaves on a thick tree, some fall, and some grow; So is the generation of flesh and blood: One comes to an end, and another is born.
Every work rots and eats away, And the worker of it shall go likewise.
Baruḵ is the man who meditates on goodness in wisdom, And thinks upon qodesh matters with his understanding.
He who considers her ways in his heart, Shall also have understanding of her secrets.
Go after her as one that follows, and lie in wait on her ways.
He who peers in her windows shall also listen at her doors.
He who lodges near her house shall also fasten a peg on her walls.
He shall pitch his tent near to her, And shall lodge in a lodging where goodness is.
He shall put his children under her shelter, And shall lodge under her branches.
By her he shall be covered from heat, And in her esteem he shall dwell.
He who reveres 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall do good, And he who has the knowledge of the Law shall obtain her.
And as a mother she shall meet him, And receive him as a wife married in maidenhood.
With the bread of understanding she shall feed him, And give him the water of wisdom to drink.
He shall be visited by her, and shall not be moved; And shall rely on her, and shall not be ashamed.
She shall exalt him above his neighbours, And she shall open his mouth in the midst of the assembly.
He shall find joy and a crown of gladness, And she shall cause him to inherit an everlasting name.
But foolish men shall not obtain her, And sinners shall not see her.
For she is far from pride, And men that are liars cannot remember her.
Praise is not fitting for the mouth of a sinner, For it was not sent to him by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
For praise shall be uttered in wisdom, And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall make it prosper.
Do not say, “It is because of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 that I fell away.” For you ought not to do that which He hates.
Do not say, “He has caused me to stray.” For He has no need of the sinful man.
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 hates all abomination; And those who revere Elohim do not love it.
He Himself made man from the beginning, And left him in the hand of his own counsel;
So you shall guard the Commands, And act trustworthily.
He has put fire and water before you; Stretch out your hand to which you choose.
Ḥai and death is before man; And what he chooses shall be given him.
For the wisdom of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is great, And He is mighty in power, and sees all.
And His eyes are upon those who revere Him, And He knows every work of man.
He has commanded no man to do wickedly, Neither has He given any man permission to sin.
Do not desire a great number of worthless children, Neither delight in wicked sons.
Though they increase, do not rejoice in them, Unless the reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is with them.
Do not trust in them living, neither regard their great number; For one that is righteous is better than a thousand; And it is better to die without children, than to have those who are wicked.
For by one that has understanding the city shall be filled; But the offspring of the wicked shall be quickly laid waste.
Many such matters I have seen with my eyes, And my ear has heard greater than these.
In the assembly of the wicked a fire shall be kindled; And in a rebellious nation wrath is lit on fire.
He was not appeased toward the giants of old, Who fell in the strength of their foolishness.
Neither did He spare the place where Lot sojourned, But loathed them for their pride.
He had no compassion for the people of destruction, Who were taken away in their sins;
Nor the six hundred thousand foot soldiers, Who were gathered together in the hardness of their hearts.
And if there is one stiff-necked among the people, It is marvel if he escapes unpunished; For kindness and wrath are with Him. He is mighty to forgive, and to pour out displeasure.
As His kindness is great, so is His discipline also. He judges a man according to his works.
The sinner shall not escape with his plunder; And the patience of the righteous shall not be defeated.
Make room for every act of kindness; For everyone shall receive according to his works.
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 hardened Pharaoh, that he should not know Him, That His mighty works might be known to the world.
His kindness is revealed to every creature; And He has separated His light from the darkness and is unbreakable.
Do not say, “I shall hide myself from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄. “Shall any remember me from above? “I shall not be remembered among so many people; “For what is my being among such a limitless number of creatures?”
See, the shamayim, and the shamayim of shamayim, The deep, and the earth, and all that is in it, Shall be moved at His visitation.
The mountains and foundations of the earth shall also be shaken with trembling, When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 looks upon them.
No heart may think upon these worthily; And who is able to perceive His ways?
It is a whirlwind that no man sees; For most of his works are hidden.
Who shall declare the works of His righteousness? Or who shall endure them? For His decree is far off, And the trial of all is at the end.
He who lacks understanding shall think upon emptiness; And a foolish man straying plots foolishness.
My son, listen to me and learn knowledge, And know my words in your heart.
I shall present instruction by measure, And declare His knowledge exactly.
The works of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 are done in right-ruling from the beginning; And from the time He made them He laid out their parts.
He decorated His works forever, And in His hand are the beginning of them to all generations; They neither labour, nor are weary, nor cease from their works.
None of them withholds another, And they never disobey His word.
After this 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 looked upon the earth, And filled it with His bireḵoth.
Has He covered the face of it with all manner of living creatures; And they shall return to it again.
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 created man from the earth, And returns him to it again.
He gave them few days, and a short time, And also authority over that within it.
He gave them strength within themselves, And made them according to His image,
And put the fear of man upon all flesh, And gave him rule over beasts and birds.
They received the use of the five senses of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, And in the sixth place He gave them understanding, And in the seventh speech, an interpreter of the thoughts.
Counsel, and a tongue, and eyes, ears, and a heart, He gave them to understand.
He filled them with the knowledge of understanding, And showed them good and evil.
He put His eye on their hearts, That He might show them the greatness of His works.
He appointed them to boast in His marvellous deeds forever, That they might declare His works with understanding.
And the elect shall praise His qodesh Name.
Besides this He gave them knowledge, And the Law of Ḥai for an inheritance.
He made an everlasting Covenant with them, And gave them His Right-Rulings.
Their eyes saw the excellence of His esteem, And their ears heard His esteemed voice.
And He said to them, “Beware of all unrighteousness.” And He gave every man Command concerning his neighbour.
Their ways are ever before Him, And shall not be hid from His eyes.
Every man from his youth is given to evil; Neither could they make hearts of flesh for themselves from stony.
For in the division of the nations of the whole earth He appointed a ruler over every people; But Yisra’ĕl is the portion of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄;
Whom being His first-born, He nourishes with discipline, And giving him the light of His love, does not forsake him.
Therefore all their works are as the sun before Him, And His eyes are continually upon their ways.
None of their unrighteous deeds are hid from Him, But all their sins are before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
But 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 showing favour and knowing His workmanship, Neither left nor forsook them, but spared them.
The kind deeds of a man are as a signet with Him, And He shall guard the good deeds of man as the apple of His eye, And give repentance to His sons and daughters.
Afterwards He shall rise up and reward them, And render their recompense upon their heads.
And to those who repent, He provides a return, And comforts those whose expectancy is failing.
Return to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and leave your sins. Make your prayer before His face, and be guiltless.
Turn again to the Most High, and turn away from wickedness; For He shall lead you out of darkness into the light of peace, And intensely hate your abominations.
Who shall praise the Most High in the grave, Except for those who live and give thanks?
Thanksgiving perishes from the dead, as from one who is not; The living and perfect in heart shall praise 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
How great is the kindness of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 our Elohim, And His compassion to those who turn to Him in qodeshah!
For not all is within man, For the son of man is not incorruptible.
What is brighter than the sun, yet its light fails? So flesh and blood shall imagine evil.
He views the power of the height of the shamayim; And all men are but dust and ashes.
He who lives forever has created all in its entirety.
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 alone is righteous, And there is no other but He,
Who guides the world with the palm of His hand, And all obey His desire; For He is the Sovereign of all by His power, Dividing the qodesh from among the profane.
To whom has He given power to declare His works? And who shall find out His noble acts?
Who shall measure the strength of His excellence? And who also shall tell of His kindnesses?
As for the wondrous works of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, there is naught taken from them, Nor any that are compared to them, Nor may the expanse of them be found out.
When a man is finished, then one begins; And when he leaves, then he shall be uncertain.
What is man, and what use is he? What is his good, and what is his evil?
The number of a man’s days at the greatest are a hundred years.
As a drop of water into the sea, and a grain compared to the sand; So are a thousand years to everlasting days.
Therefore Elohim is patient with them, And pours out His kindness upon them.
He looked and saw their end to be evil; Therefore He multiplied His compassion.
The kindness of man is toward his neighbour; But the kindness of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is upon all flesh. He reproves, and disciplines, and teaches and turns them back again, as a shepherd his flock.
He has kindness on those who receive discipline, And who diligently seek after His Right-Rulings.
My son, do not blemish your good deeds, Nor use harsh words when you give.
Does the dew not relieve the heat? So a word is better than a gift.
Look, is a word not better than a gift? But both are with one showing kindness.
A fool shall reproach harshly, And a gift of the selfish consumes the eyes.
Learn before you speak, And use healing if you are ever sick.
Before judgment examine yourself, And in the day of visitation you shall find kindness.
Humble yourself before you become sick, And in the time of sins show repentance.
Let naught hinder you to pay your vow in due time, And do not delay till death to be declared right.
Before you pray, prepare yourself; And do not be as one that tries 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
Think upon the wrath that shall be in the end, And the time of vengeance, when He turns away His face.
When you have enough, remember the time of hunger: And when you are wealthy, think upon poverty and need.
From the morning until the evening the times change, And all are soon done before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
A wise man shall revere in every matter, And in the day of sinning he shall beware of trespass. But a fool does not observe time.
Every man of understanding knows wisdom, And shall baraḵ he who finds her.
Those who have understanding in words also become wise themselves, And pour forth splendid parables.
Do not pursue your lusts, But restrain yourself from your appetites.
If you give your being the desires that it pleases, It shall make you a mockery to your enemies that slander you.
Do not revel in excessive pleasure, Nor be bound by its expense.
Do not become a beggar by feasting through borrowing, When you have naught in your purse; For you shall be lying in wait for your own life, and be plotted upon.
A labourer that is given to drunkenness shall not be wealthy; And he who despises small matters shall fall little by little.
Wine and women shall cause men of understanding to fall away: And he who clings to whores shall become hardened.
Moths and worms shall have him to inherit, And a bold man shall be taken away.
He who is hasty to give credit is light- minded; And he who sins corrupts his own being.
Whoever takes pleasure in wickedness shall be condemned: But he who resists pleasures crowns his ḥai.
He who rules his tongue shall live without strife; And he who hates gossip shall have less evil.
Do not repeat to another that which is told to you, And you shall not suffer harm.
Whether to friend or enemy, do not speak of another’s life; And if you may without offense, do not reveal them.
For if he hears and sees you, So in time to come he shall hate you.
If you have heard a word, let it die with you; And be brave, it shall not burst you!
A fool struggles with a word, As a woman in labour with a child.
As an arrow that sticks in a man’s thigh, So is a word inside a fool.
Admonish a friend, it may be he has not done it; And if he has done it, that he does it no more.
Admonish your friend, it may be he has not said it; And if he has, that he does not speak it again.
Admonish a friend, for many times it is slander, And do not believe every whisper.
There is one that slips in his speech, but not from his heart; And who is he who has not offended with his tongue?
Admonish your neighbour before you threaten him; And not being wroth, give place to the Law of the Most High.
The reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is the beginning of acceptance, And wisdom obtains His love.
The knowledge of the Commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is the instruction of Ḥai: And those who do that which pleases Him, Shall receive the fruit of the tree of immortality.
The reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is complete wisdom; And in all wisdom is the doing of the Law, And the knowledge of His mightiness.
If a servant says to his master, “I shall not do as it pleases you.” Though afterward he does it, he angers him who feeds him.
The knowledge of wickedness is not wisdom, Nor at any time is insight the counsel of sinners.
There is a wickedness, and such is an abomination; And there is a fool lacking in wisdom.
He who has little understanding, and reveres Elohim, Is better than one that has much wisdom, And transgresses the Law of the Most High.
There is a delicate craftiness, and the same is unrighteous; And there is one that turns aside to make judgment appear; And there is a wise man that speaks rightly in judgment.
There is a wicked man that bows his head sadly; But inwardly he is full of deceit,
Casting down his face, and making as if he did not hear. Where he is unknown, he shall do you evil before you are aware.
And if for need of power he may cease from sinning, Yet when he finds opportunity he shall do evil.
A man may be known by his appearance, And one that has understanding, by his face when you meet him.
A man’s dress, and excessive laughter, and walk, reveal what is.
There is a reproof that is not proper; Again, some man holds his tongue, and he is wise.
It is much better to reprove, than to be wroth secretly; And he who confesses his wrong shall be preserved from harm.
How good is it, when you are reproved, to show repentance! For so you shall escape deliberate sin.
As is the lust of a eunuch to defile a maiden; So is he who executes judgment with violence.
There is one that keeps silent, and is found wise; And another by much babbling becomes hated.
Some man holds his tongue, because he has no answer: And some keep silent, knowing his time.
A wise man shall hold his tongue till he sees opportunity; But a babbler and a fool shall regard no time.
He who uses many words shall be loathed; And he who takes authority for himself in this shall be hated.
There is a sinner that has good success in evil; And there is a gain that turns to loss.
There is a gift that shall not profit you; And there is a gift whose recompense is double.
There is he who is shamed because of esteem; And there he who lifts up his head from a low estate.
There is he who buys much for a little, But repays it sevenfold.
A wise man by his words makes him beloved; But the favours of fools shall be poured out.
The gift of a fool shall do you no good when you have it; Nor that of the greedy by necessity; For he looks to receive much for one.
He gives little, and insults greatly; He opens his mouth as an accuser. Today he lends, and tomorrow he shall ask it again; Such a one is to be hated of Elohim and man.
The fool says, “I have no friends, I have no thanks for all my good deeds, And those who eat my bread speak evil of me.”
How often, and by how many shall he be mocked! For he does not know what it is to have; And it is all the same to him as if he did not have.
To slip upon a pavement is better than to slip with the tongue; So shall the fall of the wicked come speedily.
An untimely word shall always be in the mouth of the unwise.
A wise word shall be rejected when it comes from the mouth of a fool; For he shall not speak it in its season.
There is he who is hindered from sinning through poverty; And when he takes rest, he is not troubled.
There is he who destroys his own being through shame, And overthrows himself by showing partiality.
There is he who promises to his friend from shame, And makes him his enemy for naught.
A lie is an unclean stain within a man, Yet it is continually in the mouth of the unlearned.
A thief is better than a man who is known to lie: But they shall both inherit destruction.
The way of a liar is humiliation, And his shame is ever with him.
With his words a wise man shall promote himself to esteem: And he who has understanding shall please great men.
He who tills his land shall increase his heap: And he who pleases great men shall receive pardon for wrong.
Presents and bribes blind the eyes of the wise, And stop up his mouth so he cannot reprove.
Wisdom that is hidden, and treasure that is hoarded up, What profit is there in either?
Better is he who hides his folly Than a man who hides his wisdom.
Enduring patience in seeking 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, Is better than he who leads his life without a guide.
My son, have you sinned? Do so no more, But ask forgiveness for your former sins.
Flee from sin as from the face of a serpent; For if you come too close to it, it shall bite you. The teeth of it are as the teeth of a lion, Slaying the beings of men.
All wickedness is as a two-edged sword, The wounds of which cannot be healed.
Fear and wickedness shall waste wealth; Therefore the house of the proud shall be made desolate.
A prayer out of a poor man’s mouth reaches the ears of Elohim, And his right-ruling comes speedily.
He who hates to be reproved is in the path of sinners; But he who reveres 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall repent from his heart.
A learned man is known far and near; And a man of understanding knows when he slips.
He who builds his house with another man’s silver, Is like one that gathers stones for the tomb of his burial.
The assembly of the wicked is like tow wrapped together; And their end is a flame of fire to destroy them.
The way of sinners is paved with stones, But at the end of it is the pit of She’ol.
He who guards the Law of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 gains understanding from it; And the perfect reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is wisdom.
He who is not wise cannot be taught; But there is a knowledge which multiplies bitterness.
The knowledge of a wise man shall increase as a flood: And his counsel is like a pure fountain of life.
The inward parts of a fool are like a broken vessel, And he shall hold no knowledge as long as he lives.
If a skilled man hears a wise word, He commends it, and adds to it; But when one of no understanding hears it, It displeases him, and he throws it behind his back.
The talking of a fool is like a burden on the way; But favour shall be found in the lips of the wise.
They inquire at the mouth of the wise in the assembly, And they shall consider his words in their heart.
As is a house that is destroyed, so is wisdom to a fool; And the knowledge of the unwise are words without sense.
Instruction to fools is as chains on the feet, And like shackles on the right hand.
A fool lifts up his voice with laughter; But a wise man hardly smiles a little.
Learning is to a wise man as an ornament of gold, And like a bracelet upon his right arm.
The foot of a fool hurries into his house; But a diligent man is ashamed of him.
A fool shall peep at the door into the house; But he who is disciplined shall stand outside.
It is the disrespect of a man to listen at the door: But a wise man shall be grieved with the shame.
The lips of gossipers speak that which does not pertain to them; But the words of those who have understanding are weighed in the balance.
The heart of fools is in their mouth; But the mouth of the wise is in their heart.
When the wicked curses an adversary, He curses his own being.
A whisperer defiles his own being, and is hated wherever he dwells.
A lazy man is compared to a filthy stone, And all shall hiss him to shame.
An idle man is compared to the filth of a dunghill: Every man that picks it up shall shake off his hand.
An undisciplined man is the shame of his father that brought him forth; And a daughter is brought forth to his loss.
A wise daughter brings an inheritance to her husband; But she who lives dishonestly is her father’s heaviness.
She who is bold shames both her father and her husband, And they shall both despise her.
An untimely word is music in mourning; But blows and discipline by wisdom are never untimely.
Whoever teaches a fool is as one who glues a potsherd together, And as he who wakes one from a sound sleep.
He who speaks a word to a fool speaks to one in a slumber; When he has spoken a word, he shall say, “What is this word?”
If children live decently, and have means, They shall cover the lowliness of their parents.
But children, being haughty, through pride and lacking discipline, Stain the nobility of their relatives.
Weep for the dead, for he has lost the light; And weep for the fool, for he lacks understanding. Make little weeping for the dead, for he is at rest: But the life of the fool is worse than death.
Seven days men shall mourn for the dead; But all the days of his life for a fool and a wicked man.

Do not speak much with a fool, And do not go to he who has no understanding. Beware of him, lest you have trouble, And you shall never be defiled with his foolishness. Depart from him, and you shall find rest, And never be worried with madness.
What is heavier than lead? And what is its name, but a fool?
Sand, and salt, and a mass of iron, is easier to bear, Than a man without understanding.
As timber girded and bound together in a building cannot be loosed with shaking; So the heart that is established by wise counsel shall fear at no time.
A heart rested upon a thought of understanding, Is as a lovely plastering on the wall of a gallery.
Fences put on a high place shall never stand against the wind; So a fearful heart in the mind of a fool cannot stand against any fear.
He who pricks the eye makes tears fall; And he who pricks the heart makes it show her knowledge.
Whoever throws a stone at the birds frightens them away; And he who reproaches his friend breaks a friendship.
Though you draw a sword against your friend, yet do not despair; For there may be a returning.

If you have opened your mouth against your friend, Do not fear; For there may be an atonement, Except for reproach, or pride, or disclosing secrets, or a deadly wound; For these matters every friend shall depart.

Be trustworthy to your neighbour in his poverty, That you may rejoice in his prosperity. Remain steadfast with him in the time of his distress, That you may be heir with him in his inheritance; For a poor position is not always to be despised; Nor the wealthy, who are foolish to be held in admiration.
As the clouds and smoke of a furnace goes before the fire; So reviling before blood.
I shall not be ashamed to defend a friend; Nor shall I hide myself from him.
But if any evil comes upon me because of him, Every one that hears it shall beware of him.
Who shall appoint a guard before my mouth, And a seal of wisdom upon my lips, So I do not suddenly fall by them, And that my tongue does not destroy me?
O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, Father and Aḏon of all my ḥai, Do not leave me to their counsels, And do not let me fall by them.
Who shall appoint whips over my thoughts, And the discipline of wisdom over my heart? That they do not spare me for my ignorances, And it does not pass by my sins;
Lest my ignorances increase, and my sins multiply to my destruction, And I fall before my adversaries, and my enemy rejoice over me, Whose expectancy is far from Your kindness.
O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, Father and Elohim of my ḥai, Do not give me a proud look, But always turn your servants away from a haughty mind.
Turn me away from worthless expectation and lust, And You hold up he who desires to always serve You.
Do not let the gluttony of the stomach nor lust of the flesh take hold of me; And do not give me, your servant, over to a hardened heart.
Hear O you children, the instruction of the mouth; He who guards it shall never be overtaken with his lips.
The sinner shall be left in his foolishness; Both the speaker of evil and the proud shall fall by it.
Do not accustom your mouth to swearing; Nor use the Name of the Qadosh One.
For as a servant that is continually beaten shall not be without a bruise; So he who swears Naming Elohim continually shall not be guiltless.

A man that swears much is filled with wickedness, And the plague shall never depart from his house. If he transgresses, his sin shall be upon him; And if he does not acknowledge his sin, he commits a double offense: And if he swears in vain, he shall not be innocent, But his house shall be filled with calamities.

There is a word that is clothed with death; Elohim grant that it not be found in the inheritance of Ya’aqoḇ; For all such matters shall be far from the reverent, And they shall not wallow In their sins.
Do not use your mouth to swear rashly, For in these words there is sin.

Remember your father and your mother when you sit among great men. Do not be forgetful before them, and so, by your habit, Become a fool, and wish that you had not been born, And curse the day of your birth.
The man who is accustomed to insulting words Shall never be instructed all the days of his life.

Two kinds of men multiply sin, and the third shall bring wrath: A heated spirit as a burning fire shall never be quenched till it is consumed: One who whores in the body of his flesh shall never cease till he has kindled a fire.
All bread is sweet to those who whore, He does not cease till he dies.
An adulterer, says thus in his heart: “Who sees me? I am surrounded with darkness. “The walls cover me, and no one sees me; what do I need to fear? “The Most High shall not remember my sins.”
Such a man only fears the eyes of men, And does not know that the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 are ten thousand times brighter than the sun, Watching all the ways of men, and observing the most secret places.
He knew all when they were created; So after they were accomplished he looked upon them all.
This man shall be punished in the streets of the city, And he shall be taken where he does not suspect.
So it shall also be for the wife that leaves her husband, And brings forth an heir by another.

For firstly, she has disobeyed the Law of the Most High; And secondly, she has trespassed against her own husband; And thirdly, she has committed whoring by adultery, And brought forth children by another man.
She shall be brought out into the assembly, And inquiry shall be made of her children.
Her children shall not take root, And her branches shall not bring forth fruit.
She shall leave a cursed remembrance, And her reproach shall not be blotted out.
And those who remain shall know that there is none better than the reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, And that there is naught sweeter than to guard the Commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
It is great esteem to follow 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, And to be accepted by Him is long life.
Wisdom shall praise herself, And be esteemed in the midst of her people.
In the assembly of the Most High she opens her mouth, And overcomes before His power.
I came out of the mouth of the Most High, And covered the earth as a cloud.
I dwelt in high places, And my throne is in a cloudy pillar.
I alone surrounded the circuit of the shamayim, And walked in the bottom of the deep.
In the waves of the sea and in all the earth, And in every people and nation, I obtained a possession.
