With all these I sought rest; And in whose inheritance shall I remain?
So the Creator of all gave me a command, And He who made me gave rest for my tent, and said, “Let your dwelling be in Ya’aqoḇ, and your inheritance in Yisra’ĕl.”
He created me from the beginning before the world, And I shall never fail.
In the qodesh Mishkan I served before Him; And so I was established in Tsiyon.
Likewise in the beloved city He gave me rest, And in Yerushalayim was my strength.
And I took root in an esteemed people, Even in the portion of the inheritance of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
I was exalted like a cedar in Leḇanon, And as a cypress upon the mountains of Ḥermon.
I was exalted like a palm tree in Ĕyn Geḏi, And as a rosebush in Yeriḥo, As a fair olive tree in a pleasant field, And grew as a fig tree by the water.

I gave a sweet smell like cinnamon and rosewood, And I yielded a pleasant fragrance like the best myrrh, As galbanam, and shoham, and fragrant gum, And as the fragrance of frankincense in the Mishkan.
As the cypress I stretched out my branches, And my branches are the branches of esteem and favour.
As the vine I brought forth a pleasant fragrance, And my flowers are the fruit of esteem and wealth.
I am the mother of pleasant love, and reverence, and knowledge, and qodesh expectancy: I therefore, being of old, Am given to all my children who are named by Him.
Come to me, all you who desire me, And fill yourselves with my fruit.
For my remembrance is sweeter than honey, And my inheritance than the honeycomb.
Those who eat of me shall hunger for more, And those who drink me shall thirst for more.
He who obeys me shall never be ashamed, And those who work beside me shall not do wrong.
All these are the Book of the Covenant of the Most High Elohim, Even the Law which Mosheh Commanded for an inheritance to the congregations of Ya’aqoḇ.
Do not lose heart, but be strong in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, that He may confirm you; Cling to Him, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Almighty is Elohim alone, And beside Him there is no other Saviour.
He fills all with His wisdom, As Pishon and as Ḥiddeqel in the time of first- fruits.
He makes understanding to abound like Perath, And as the Yardĕn in the time of the harvest.
He makes the instruction of knowledge appear as the light, And as Giḥon in the time of grape harvest.
The first man did not know her fully; Nor shall the last find her out.
For her thoughts are more than the sea, And her counsels deeper than the great deep.
I also came out as a wadi from a river, And as a channel into a garden.
I said, “I shall water my best garden, And shall water my garden bed very much.” And see, my wadi became a river, and my river became a sea.
I shall yet make instruction to shine as the morning, And shall send forth her light far away.
I shall yet pour out instruction as neḇuah, And leave it to all ages forever.
See that I have not laboured for myself only, But for all those who seek wisdom.
In three matters I was adorned, And stood in loveliness both before Elohim and man: The oneness of brothers, the love of neighbours, A man and wife that agree together.
Three sorts of men my being hates, And I greatly loathe of their life: A poor man who is proud, a wealthy man who is a liar, And an old adulterer who is foolish.
If you have gathered naught in your youth, How shall you find any matter in your old age?
O how lovely is judgment for grey hairs, And for the aged to know counsel!
O how lovely is the wisdom of old men, And understanding and counsel in men of esteem.
Much experience is the crown of old men, And the reverence of Elohim is their esteem.
There are nine which I have judged in my heart to be baruḵ, And the tenth I shall relate with my tongue: A man that has joy from his children; And he who lives to see the fall of his enemy.
Good is he who dwells with a wife of understanding, And that has not slipped with his tongue, And that has not served a man more unworthy than himself.
Good is he who has found insight, And he who speaks in the ears of those who listen.
O how great is he who finds wisdom! Yet there is none above he who reveres 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
But the love of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 passes all in understanding; He who possesses it, to what shall he be likened?
The reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is the beginning of His love; And belief is the beginning of clinging to Him.
Any wound, but a wound of the heart; And any wickedness, but the wickedness of a woman.
And any affliction, but the affliction from those who hate me; And any revenge, but the revenge of enemies.
There is no venom above the venom of a serpent; And there is no wrath above the wrath of an enemy.
I would rather dwell with a lion and a dragon, Than to dwell in a house with a wicked woman.
The wickedness of a woman changes her appearance, And darkens her face like sackcloth.
Her husband shall sit among his neighbours; And listening he shall sigh bitterly.
All wickedness is but little to the wickedness of a woman; Let the portion of a sinner fall upon her.
As the climbing of a sandy way is to the feet of the aged, So is a wife full of words to a quiet man.
Do not stumble at the loveliness of a woman, And do not desire her for pleasure.
A woman supporting her husband, Is full of wrath, hardness, and much reproach.
A wicked woman causes courage to cease, Causes a heavy face and a wounded heart; A woman that does not comfort her husband in distress Causes weak hands and feeble knees.
From the woman came the beginning of sin, And because of her we all die.
Give water no outlet; Nor a wicked woman freedom to roam.
If she does not do as you would have her, Cut her off from yourself, And give her a certificate of divorce, and let her go.
Baruḵ is the man that has a capable wife, For the number of his days shall be double.
A capable woman gladdens her husband, And he shall fill the years of his life in peace.
A good wife is a good portion, Which shall be given in the portion of those who revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
Whether a man is wealthy or poor, If he has a good heart toward 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, He shall rejoice at all times with a cheerful face.

There are three matters that my heart fears; And of the fourth I was very afraid: The slander of a city, the gathering together of an unruly crowd, and a false accusation; All these are worse than death.
But a woman that is jealous over another woman is grieving to the heart and sorrow; And a lashing tongue which makes known to all.
An evil wife is a yoke shaken to and fro; He who has hold of her is as though he held a scorpion.
A drunken and wandering woman causes great wrath, And she does not cover her own shame.
The whoring of a woman is known by her haughty looks and eyelids.
If your daughter is wayward, keep her straight, Lest she abuse herself through too much freedom.
Watch over one with a hard eye; And do not marvel if she trespasses against you.
She shall open her mouth, as a thirsty traveller who has found a fountain, And drink of every water near her. By every hedge she shall sit down, And open her quiver for every arrow.
The favour of a wife delights her husband, And her discretion shall fatten his bones.
A silent and loving woman is a gift of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄; And there is naught worth as much as a mind well instructed.
A humble and trustworthy woman is a double favour, And her sober mind cannot be valued.
As the sun when it rises high in the shamayim; So is the loveliness of a good wife in the ordering of her house.
As the shining light upon the qodesh candlestick; So is the loveliness of the face in ripe age.
As the golden stands upon the sockets of silver; So are the lovely feet with a constant heart.
My son, guard the flower of your youth well; And do not give your strength to foreigners.
When you have acquired a fruitful possession through all the field, Sow it with your own seed, trusting in the goodness of your stock.
So your relatives which you leave are made great, Having the confidence of their good genealogy.
A whore shall be counted as spittle; But a married woman is a tower against death to her husband.
A wicked woman is given as a portion to a wicked man; But a reverent woman is given to he who reveres 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
A dishonest woman is despised and shamed; But an honest woman shall revere her husband.
A headstrong woman shall be counted as a dog; But she that is humble reveres 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
A woman that esteems her husband shall be judged wise among all; But she that shames him in her pride shall be counted wicked among all.
A loud-mouthed woman and a nagger shall be sought out to drive away the enemies.

There are two matters that grieve my heart; And the third makes me wroth: A man of battle that suffers poverty; And men of understanding that are not respected; And one that turns from righteousness to sin; 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 prepares such a one for the sword.
A merchant hardly guards himself from doing wrong; And a trader is not free from sin.
Many have sinned for a small matter; And he who seeks abundance turns his eyes away.
As a nail holds fast between the join of stones; So sin holds close between buying and selling.
Unless a man behaves diligently in the reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, His house shall soon be overthrown.
As when one sifts with a sieve, the refuse remains; So the filth of man is in his words.
The furnace tries the potter’s vessels; So the trial of man is in his reasoning.
The fruit declares if the tree has been cultivated; So is the speaking of pride in the heart of man.
Praise no man before you hear him speak; For this is the trial of men.
If you follow righteousness, you shall obtain it, And put it on, as a long robe of esteem.
The birds shall gather with their kind; So shall truth return to those who practise it.
As the lion lies in wait for prey; So does sin for those who work wickedness.
The words of a reverent man are always with wisdom; But a fool changes as the moon.
Watch the time if you are among the foolish; But be continually among men of understanding.
The words of fools are troublesome, And their entertainment is the indecency of sin.
The words of he who swears much makes the hair stand upright; And their uproar makes one stop his ears.
The strife of the proud is bloodshed, And their revilings are grievous to the ear.
Whoever uncovers secrets loses his trust; And shall never find a friend of his being.
Love your friend, and be trustworthy to him; But if you betray his secrets, never again follow after him.
For as a man has destroyed his enemy; So you have lost the love of your neighbour.
As one that releases a bird out of his hand, So you have let your neighbour go, And shall not have him again.
Do not follow after him, for he is too far off; He is like a gazelle escaped out of the snare.
As for a wound, it may be bound up, And after reviling there may be peace; But he who betrays secrets is without expectancy.
He who winks with the eyes works evil; And he who knows him departs from him.
When you are present, he shall speak sweetly, and shall admire your words; But in the end he shall twist his mouth, and slander your sayings.
I have hated many matters, but naught like him; For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall hate him.
Whoever throws a stone high, throws it on his own head; And a blow in deceit makes wounds.
Whoever digs a pit shall fall in to it; And he who lays a trap shall be caught in it.
He who does evil, it shall fall upon him, And he shall not know from where it comes.
Mockery and reproach are from the proud; But vengeance as a lion, lies in wait for them.
Those who rejoice at the fall of the righteous shall be taken in the snare; And anguish shall consume them before they die.
Evil and wrath, even these are abominations; And the sinful man has them both.
He who is vengeful shall find vengeance from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, And He shall surely keep account of his sins.
Forgive your neighbour the harm that he has done to you, So your sins shall also be forgiven when you pray.
One man bears hatred against another, And should he seek forgiveness from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄?
He shows no kindness to a man, who is like himself; And does he ask forgiveness of his own sins?
If he who is but flesh maintains hatred, Who shall pray forgiveness for his sins?
Remember your end, and let enmity cease; Corruption and death, and remain in the Commands.
Remember the Commands, and bear no evil against your neighbour; The Covenant of the Most High, and overlook faults.
Abstain from strife, and you shall diminish your sins; For a man of rage kindles strife,
A sinful man disrupts friendships, And creates quarrels among those who are at peace.

As the structure of the fire, so it burns: And as a man’s strength is, so is his wrath; And according to his wealth his wrath rises; And the stronger they are who contend, The more they shall be inflamed.
A hasty quarrel kindles a fire; And hasty fighting sheds blood.
If you blow the spark, it shall burn; If you spit upon it, it shall be quenched; And both of these come out of your mouth.
Curse the gossiper and double tongued; For such have destroyed many who were at peace.
A backbiting tongue has troubled many, and driven them from nation to nation: It has pulled down strong cities, and overthrown the houses of great men.
A backbiting tongue has thrown out virtuous women, And deprived them of their labours.
Whoever listens to it shall never find rest, and never dwell quietly.
The stroke of the whip makes marks in the flesh; But the stroke of the tongue breaks the bones.
Many have fallen by the edge of the sword; But not as many who have fallen by the tongue.
It is good for he who is protected from its venom; Who has not drawn its yoke, nor been bound in its bands.
For its yoke is a yoke of iron, And its bands are bands of bronze.
The death from it is an evil death; The grave is better than it.
It shall not rule over those who revere Elohim, Nor shall they be burned with its flame.
Those who forsake 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall fall into it; And it shall burn in them, and not be quenched. It shall be sent upon them as a lion, And devour them as a leopard.
As you hedge your possessions with thorns around, And bind up your silver and gold,
Weigh your words in a balance, And make a door and bar for your mouth.
Beware you do not slip by it, Lest you fall before he who lies in wait.
He who is kind shall lend to his neighbour; And he who strengthens his hand guards the Commands.
Lend to your neighbour in his time of need, And repay your neighbour again in due season.
Guard your word, and deal trustworthily with him, And you shall always find that which is necessary for you.
Many reckon what was loaned to them to be found, And put to trouble those who helped them.

Till he has received, he shall kiss a man’s hand; And for his neighbour’s silver he shall speak softly; But when he should repay, he shall prolong the time, And return words of grief, and complain of the time.

If he overcomes, he shall hardly give the half, And he shall count it as though he had found it. If not, he has deprived him of his silver, and he has gained an enemy without cause. He pays him with cursings and slander; And instead of esteem he shall pay him shame.
Many have therefore refused to lend for other men’s evil deeds, Fearing to be cheated.
Yet have patience with a man in poverty, And do not delay to show him kindness.
Help the poor for the sake of the Command, And do not turn him away because of his poverty.
Lose your silver for your brother and your friend, And do not let it rust under a stone to be lost.
Lay up your treasure according to the Commands of the Most High, And it shall bring you more profit than gold.
Store up kind deeds in your storehouses, And it shall deliver you from all affliction.
It shall fight for you against your enemies better than a mighty shield and strong spear.
An honest man stands guarantor for his neighbour; But he who is impudent shall forsake him.
Do not forgot the friendship of your guarantor, For he has given his life for you.
A sinner shall overthrow the good manner of his guarantor;
And he who is thankless shall forsake he who delivered him.
Guarantee has undone many of good estate, And shaken them as a wave of the sea. It has driven mighty men from their houses, So that they wandered among foreign nations.
A wicked man transgressing the Commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall fall in guarantee; And he who undertakes and follows other men’s business for gain shall fall into lawsuits.
Assist your neighbour according to your ability, And beware that you do not fall into the same.
The necessities for life are water, and bread, and garments, And a house for privacy.
Better is the life of a poor man in a lowly cottage, Than food of delicacies in another man’s house.
Whether little or much, be content, That you do not hear the reproach of your house.
For it is a miserable life to go from house to house; For where you are a stranger, you dare not open your mouth.
You shall entertain, and feast, and have no thanks; And you shall hear bitter words:
“Come, you stranger, and furnish a table, And feed me of what you have ready.
“Give place, you stranger, to an esteemed man; My brother seeks lodging, and I have need of my house.”
These matters are grievous to a man of understanding; The contempt of a household, and a reproach of the lender.
He who loves his son causes him to often feel the rod, That he may have joy from him in the end.
He who punishes his son shall have joy in him, And shall rejoice in him among his acquaintances.
He who teaches his son grieves the enemy; And before his friends he shall rejoice in him.
Though his father dies, it is as though he were not dead; For he has left one behind who is like himself.
While he lived, he saw and rejoiced in him: And when he died, he was not grieved.
He left behind an avenger against his enemies, And one that shall repay kindness to his friends.
He who makes too much of his son binds up his wounds; And his body shall be troubled at every cry.
A horse unbroken becomes headstrong: And a child left to himself shall be unruly.
Spoil your child, and he shall cause you dread; Play with him, and he shall bring you to grief.
Do not laugh with him, lest you have sorrow from him, And lest you gnash your teeth in the end.
Give him no freedom in his youth, And do not wink at his foolishness.
Bow down his neck while he is young, And beat his side while he is a child, Lest he become stubborn, and be disobedient to you, And so bring sorrow to your heart.
Discipline your son, and put him to work, Lest his wicked behaviour be a stumbling to you.
Better is the poor, being healthy and strong in body, Than a wealthy man who is afflicted in his body.
Health and good state of body are better than any gold, And a strong body above infinite wealth.
There is no wealth above a healthy body, And no joy above the joy of the heart.
Death is better than a bitter life or continual sickness.
Delicacies poured upon a closed mouth, Are as servings of meat placed upon a grave.
What good is the offering to an idol? For it neither eats nor smells; So is he who is persecuted by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
He sees with his eyes and groans, As a eunuch that embraces a maiden and sighs.
Do not give your mind over to sorrow, And do not afflict yourself on purpose.
The gladness of the heart is the life of man, And the joy of a man prolongs his days.
Love your own being, and comfort your heart. Remove sorrow far from you; For sorrow has killed many, and there is no profit in it.
Envy and wrath shorten the life, And worry brings age before time.
A cheerful and good heart pays attention to his meat and diet.
Watching for wealth consumes the flesh, And the worry of it drives away sleep.
Watchful worry does not let a man slumber, As a painful disease breaks sleep.
The wealthy labours greatly in gathering wealth together; And when he rests, he is filled with his delicacies.
The poor labours in his poverty; And when he finishes, he is still needy.
He who loves gold shall not be declared right, And he who pursues corruption shall have enough.
Gold has been the ruin of many, And their destruction stands.
It is a stumbling block to those who offer to it, And every fool shall be taken in it.
Baruḵ is the wealthy who is found without blemish, And has not gone after gold.
Who is he, that we may call him baruḵ? For he has done wonders among his people.
Who has been tried by it, and found perfect? Then let him boast. Who might offend, and has not offended? Or may do evil, and has not done it?
His goods shall be established, And the assembly shall declare his kind deeds.
If you sit at a plentiful table, do not be greedy on it, And do not say, “There is much food on it.”
Remember that an evil eye is wickedness; And what is created more evil than an eye? Therefore it weeps at every occasion.
Do not stretch your hand wherever you look, And do not thrust with it into the dish.
Do not judge your neighbour by yourself; But be discerning in every matter.
Eat as is allowed, that which is put before you; But do not devour, lest you be hated.
For the sake of manners, be first to cease; And do not be gluttonous, lest you cause stumbling.
When you sit among many, Do not be the first to reach out your hand.
A very little is sufficient for a man of discipline, And he is not short of breath on his bed.
Sound sleep comes from moderate eating; He rises early, and is attentive; But the pain of worry, and bitterness, and stomach pangs, Are with a gluttonous man.
And if you have been forced to eat, Rise up, go vomit, and you shall have rest.
My son, listen to me, and do not despise me, And in the end you shall find as I told you. In all your work be efficient, so that no sickness comes to you.
Whoever is generous with his food, men shall speak well of him; And the report of his good hospitality shall be believed.
But against he who is greedy with his food, the whole city shall murmur; And the report of his selfishness shall not be doubted.
Do not show your boldness with wine; For wine has destroyed many.
The furnace proves the sword edge by dipping; So wine tries the hearts of the proud in drunkenness.
Wine is as good as life to a man, if it is drunk moderately. What then is life to a man that is without wine? For it was made to make men glad.
Wine drunk moderately and in season brings gladness of the heart, And cheerfulness of the mind;
But wine drunken in excess makes bitterness of the mind, With brawling and quarreling.
Drunkenness increases the rage of a fool till he stumbles: It diminishes strength, and causes wounds.
Do not rebuke your neighbour while at wine, And do not despise him in his rejoicing; Give him no words of grief, and do not urge him on.
If you are appointed master do not lift yourself up, But be among them as one of the rest. Diligently look after them, and then sit down.
And when you have fulfilled your office, take your place, That you may rejoice with them, And receive a crown for your well ordering of the feast.
Speak, you who are the elder, for it is fitting for you, But with right-ruling; and do not withhold music.
Do not pour out words when there is a musician, And do not put forth wisdom out of time.
A concert of music at a banquet of wine is as a signet of ruby mounted in gold.
As a signet of an emerald mounted in a work of gold, So is the melody of music with pleasant wine.
Speak, young man, if there is need of you; And yet only twice when you are asked.
Let your words be few, saying much with few words; Be as one who knows and yet holds his tongue.
If you are among great men, do not make yourself equal with them; And when aged men are in place, do not use many words.
Before the thunder goes lightning; And before a humble man goes favour.
Rise up early, and do not be the last; And get home without delay.
There fulfill your office, and do what you shall: But do not sin with proud speech.
And for these baraḵ He who made you, And has filled you with His goodness.
Whoever reveres 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall receive His discipline; And those who seek Him early shall find favour.
He who seeks the Law shall be filled with it; But the hypocrite shall stumble over it.
Those who revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall find Right-Ruling, And shall kindle righteousness as a light.
A sinful man shall not be reproved, But finds an excuse according to his liking.
A man of counsel is considerate; But a strange and proud man is not troubled by fear, Even when he himself has done without counsel.
Do no deed without advice; And when you are done, do not regret it.
Do not go in a way in which you may fall, And do not stumble among the stones.
Do not be reckless on an easy road.
And beware of your own children.
In every good work guard your own being; For this is the keeping of the Commands.
He who believes in 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 guards the Commands; And he who trusts in Him does not come to harm.
No evil shall come upon he who reveres 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄; And in trials He also shall deliver him.
A wise man does not hate the Law; But he who is a hypocrite in it, is like a ship in a storm.
A man of understanding trusts in the Law; And the Law is trustworthy to him, as a Word.
Prepare what to say, and so you shall be heard; And draw upon instruction, and then give answer.
The heart of the foolish is like a cartwheel; And his thoughts are like a rolling axle.
A mocking friend is like a stallion, He neighs under everyone that rides him.
Why is one day better than another, When all the light of every day of the year is from the sun?
By the knowledge of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 they were appointed; And He turns seasons and Feasts.
Some of them He has made High Days, and qadosh them, And some of them He has made regular days.
And all men are from the ground, And Aḏam was created from the earth.
In much knowledge 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has spread them, And made their ways different.
Some of them He has baraḵ and exalted, And some of them He qadosh, and placed near Himself; But some of them He has cursed and brought low, And removed from their places.
As the clay is in the potter’s hand, to fashion it at his desire; So is man in the hand of He who made him, To give unto them as He thinks best.
Good opposes evil, and life against death; So is the righteous against the sinner, and the wicked against the reverent.
So look upon all the works of the Most High; And there are pairs of two, one against another.
I woke up last of all, as one that gathers after the grape gatherers; By the beraḵah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 I profited, and trod my winepress like a gatherer of grapes.
Consider that I did not labour for myself only, But for all those who seek learning.
Hear me, O you great men of the people, And listen with your ears, you rulers of the assembly.
Do not give your son and wife, your brother and friend, power over you while you live, And do not give your goods to another; Lest you reconsider, and you ask for its return.
As long as you live and have breath in you, Do not give yourself over to any.
For it is better that your children should seek from you, Than that you should stand to their sympathy.
Be the best in all your works; Do not leave a blot on your esteem.
At the time when you shall end your days, and finish your life, Distribute your inheritance.
Fodder, a rod, and burdens, are for the donkey; And bread, discipline, and work, for a servant.
If you put your servant to labour, you shall find rest: But if you let him go idle, he shall seek freedom.
A yoke and a collar bow the neck; So are tortures and punishment for an evil servant.
Send him to work, so he is not idle; For idleness teaches much evil.
Put him to work, as is fit for him; If he is not obedient, put on heavier shackles.
But do not be excessive toward any; And do naught without discretion.
If you have a servant, let him be to you as yourself, Because you have bought him for a price.
If you have a servant, treat him as a brother; For you have need of him, as of your own being. If you treat him evilly, and he runs from you, Which way shall you go to seek him?
The expectancies of a man of no understanding are empty and false; And dreams raise up fools.
Whoever regards dreams is like he who catches at a shadow, And follows after the wind.
The vision of dreams is the reflection of one to another, Even as the likeness of a face to a face.
From an unclean matter, what may be cleansed? And from that which is false, what truth shall come?
Divination, and predictions, and dreams, are empty; And imaginations of the heart, As the heart of a woman in childbirth.
If they are not sent from the Most High in your visitation, Do not lay your heart upon them.
For dreams have deceived many, And they have failed those who put their trust in them.
The Law shall be found perfect without falsehood; And wisdom is perfection to a trustworthy mouth.
A man that has travelled knows much; And he who has much experience shall declare wisdom.
He who has no experience knows little; But he who has travelled is full of insight.
When I travelled, I saw much; And I understand more than I could express.
I was often in danger of death; Yet I was delivered because of these:
The spirit of those who revere 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall live; For their expectancy is in He who saves them.
Whoever reveres 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall not fear nor be afraid; For He is his expectancy.
Baruḵ is the being of he who reveres 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄: To whom does he look, and who is his strength?

For the eyes of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 are upon those who love Him, He is their mighty shield and strong support, A protection from heat, and a cover from the sun at noon, A preservation from stumbling, and a help from falling.
He raises up the being, and lightens the eyes: He gives health, ḥai, and beraḵah.
He who offers of what is wrongfully gotten, his offering is a mockery; And the gifts of unrighteous men are not accepted.
The Most High is not pleased with the offerings of the wicked; Nor is He appeased by the multitude of offerings for sin.
Whoever brings an offering from the goods of the poor, Does as one that kills the son before his father’s eyes.
The bread of the needy is their life; He who deprives him of it is a man of blood.
He who takes away the livelihood of his neighbour slays him; And he who deprives the labourer of his wage is a shedder of blood.
When one builds, and another pulls down, What profit do they have but labour?
When one prays, and another curses, Whose voice shall 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 hear?
He who washes himself after touching a dead body, If he touches it again, what use is his washing?
So it is with a man that fasts for his sins, and goes again, and does the same; Who shall hear his prayer, or what does his humbling profit him?
He who guards the Law brings offerings enough; He who guards the Command offers a peace offering.
He who repays a good deed offers fine flour; And he who gives in kindness offers praise.
To depart from wickedness is pleasing to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄; And to forsake unrighteousness is an atonement.
You shall not appear empty-handed before 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
For all these are because of the Command.
The offering of the righteous makes the altar fat, And its sweet savour is before the Most High.
The offering of a righteous man is acceptable. And the remembrance of it shall never be forgotten.
Give 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 His esteem with a good eye, And do not diminish the first-fruits of your hands.
In all your gifts show a cheerful face, And dedicate your tithes with gladness.
Give to the Most High according to His enrichment unto you; And as you have received, give with a cheerful eye.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 repays, And shall give you seven times as much.
Do not think to corrupt with gifts; for He does not accept these: And do not trust in unrighteous offerings; For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is Judge, and with Him is no partiality.
He shows no partiality against the poor, But shall hear the prayer of the oppressed.
He shall not despise the prayer of the fatherless; Nor the widow, when she pours out her complaint.
Do not the tears run down the widow’s cheeks? And is not her cry against he who causes them to fall?
He who 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 serves shall be accepted with favour, And his prayer reaches to the clouds.
The prayer of the humble pierces the clouds; And he shall not be comforted till it comes near; And shall not depart, till the Most High executes right- ruling and judgment.

For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 does not delay, nor is the Almighty patient toward them, Till He has crushed the loins of the ruthless, And repaid vengeance upon the gentiles; Till He has taken away the crowd of the proud, And broken the sceptre of the unrighteous;
Till He has given to everyone according to their deeds, And to the works of men according to their schemes; Till He has judged the cause of His people, And caused them to rejoice in His kindness.
Favour is welcomed in the time of affliction, As clouds of rain in the time of drought.
Show favour upon us, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of all, and look on us;
And send Your fear upon all the nations that do not seek You.
Lift up Your hand against the foreign nations, And let them see Your strength.
As You were qadosh in us before them: So You be exalted among them before us.
And let them know You, as we have known You, That there is no Elohim but You alone, O Elohim.
Show new signs, and make other awesome wonders; Esteem Your hand and Your right arm, That they may put forth Your wondrous works.
Raise up displeasure, and pour out wrath; Remove the adversary, and destroy the enemy.
Shorten the time, remember the Covenant, And let them declare Your wonders.
Let he who escapes be consumed by the rage of the fire; And let those who oppress the people perish.
Crush the heads of the rulers of the gentiles that say, “There is no one else but us!”
Gather all the tribes of Ya’aqoḇ together; Your inheritance, as from the beginning.
O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, show favour upon the people that are called by Your Name, And upon Yisra’ĕl, whom You have named Your first- born.
O be kind to Yerushalayim, Your qodesh city, The place of Your rest.
Fill Tsiyon with Your unspeakable words, And Your people with Your esteem.
Give witness to those who You have possessed from the beginning, And raise up neḇi’im that are for Your Name.
Reward those who wait for You, And let Your neḇi’im be found trustworthy.
O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, hear the prayer of Your servants, According to the beraḵah of Aharon over Your people, That all those who dwell on the earth may know that You are 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, The Elohim of old.
The stomach consumes all foods, Yet one meat is better than another.
As the mouth tastes different kinds of game; So does a heart of understanding false speeches.
A crooked heart causes grief; But a man of experience shall repay him.
A woman shall accept any man, Yet one daughter is better than another.
The loveliness of a woman cheers the face, And there is naught a man loves better.
If there is kindness, meekness, and comfort, in her tongue, Then her husband is not like other men.
He who acquires a wife begins a possession, A help like himself, and a pillar of rest.
Where no wall is, there possessions are plundered; And he who has no wife shall wander about sighing.
Who shall trust a crafty thief that skips from city to city? Even so a man that has no house, and lodges wherever the night takes him?
Every friend says, “I am his friend also.” But there is a friend, which is only a friend in name.
Is it not a grief unto death, When a companion and friend is turned to an enemy?
O wicked thoughts, where have you come from, To cover the earth with deceit?
There is a companion, who rejoices in the prosperity of a friend, But in the time of trouble shall be against him.
There is a companion, who helps his friend for his stomach, And takes up a shield against the enemy.
Do not forget your friend in your heart, And do not forget him in your wealth.
Every counsellor extolls counsel; But some who counsel for themselves.
Beware of a counsellor, and know before what need he has; For he shall counsel for himself; And cast the lot against you,
And say to you, “Your way is good.” And afterward stand on the other side, to see what shall befall you.
Do not consult with one that suspects you; And hide your counsel from those who envy you.

Nor consult with a woman regarding she of whom she is jealous; Nor with a coward in matters of battle; Nor with a merchant concerning exchange; Nor with a buyer about selling; Nor with an envious man about thankfulness; Nor with a ruthless man regarding kindness; Nor with the lazy for any work; Nor with a yearly hired man about finishing work; Nor with an idle servant of much business. Do not listen to these in any matter of counsel,
But be continually with a reverent man, Whom you know to guard the Commands of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, Whose, mind is according to your mind, And shall grieve with you, if you fail.
And let the counsel of your own heart stand; For there is no man more trustworthy to you than it.
For the mind of a man sometimes tells him more than seven watchmen, That sit above in a high tower.
And above all this, pray to the Most High, That He directs your way in truth.
Let reason go before every work, And counsel before every action.
The face is a sign of changing of the heart.
Four ways of all are apparent: Good and evil, life and death; But the tongue rules over them continually.
There is one who is wise and teaches many, And yet does not profit himself.
There is one who shows wisdom in words, and is hated; He shall be destitute of all food.
For favour is not given to him from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, Because he has neglected all wisdom.
Another is wise to himself; And the fruits of understanding are as praise in his mouth.
A wise man instructs his people; And the fruits of his understanding do not fail.
A wise man shall be filled with bireḵoth; And all those who see him shall regard him as baruḵ.
The days of the life of man may be numbered; But the days of Yisra’ĕl are without number.
A wise man shall inherit esteem among his people, And his name shall be forever.
My son, prove your being in your life, And see what is evil for it, and do not give in to it.
For not all is profitable for all men, Nor has every being pleasure in every matter.
Do not be gluttonous in any delicacy, Nor too greedy with food;
For excess of food brings sickness, And gluttony shall turn to disgust.
Many have perished by gluttony; But he who guards himself prolongs his life.
Esteem a physician with the esteem due to him for the uses which you may have for him: For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has created him.
For healing comes from the Most High, And He shall receive esteem from the sovereign.
The skill of the physician shall raise his head; And in the sight of great men he shall be admired.
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has created medicines out of the earth; And he who is wise does not reject them.
Was not the water made sweet with wood, That its power might be known?
And He has given men skill, That He might be esteemed by His marvellous works.
With such He heals and takes away their pains.
Of such the perfumer makes a perfume; And of His works there is no end; And from Him there is peace over all the earth.
My son, in your sickness do not be slack; But pray to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and He shall heal you.
Cease from sin, and order your hands well, And cleanse your heart from all wickedness.
Offer a sweet fragrance, and a remembrance of fine flour; And make an offering of fat of your being.
So give place to the physician, for 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has created him; Do not let him leave you, for you have need of him.
There is a time when there is good success in their hands.
For they shall also pray to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, That He would prosper that which they give, For ease and health to prolong life.
He who sins before his Maker, Let him fall in the hand of the physician.
My son, let tears fall down over the dead, And begin to lament, as if you had suffered great harm yourself; And then cover his body according to the custom, And do not neglect his burial.
Weep bitterly, and make a great mourning with lamentation, as he is worthy, And that a day or two, lest you are spoken evil of; And then comfort yourself for your grief.
For from grief comes death, and heaviness of the heart destroys strength.
In affliction sorrow also remains; And the life of the poor is the curse of the heart.
Take no grief to heart; Drive it away, and remember the latter end.
Do not forget it, for there is no returning again; You shall do him no good, but harm yourself.
“Remember my judgment; for so shall yours be also... Yesterday for me, and today for you.”
When the dead is at rest, let his remembrance rest; And be comforted for him, when his spirit has departed from him.
The wisdom of a learned man comes by opportunity of leisure; And he who has little business may become wise.
How shall he who holds the plough attain wisdom, And who sharpens the goad, who drives oxen, and is occupied in their labour, and whose talk is of bulls?
He gives his mind to making furrows; And is diligent to give the cattle fodder.

So every carpenter and worker, that labours night and day; And those who cut and engrave seals, And are diligent to make great variety, and give themselves to copy imagery, and watch to finish a work;

Also the smith sitting by the anvil, and considering the iron work, The smoke of the fire weakens his flesh, and he fights the heat of the furnace; The noise of the hammer and the anvil is constantly in his ears, and his eyes are fixed on the pattern of that which he makes; He applies his mind to finish his work, And watches to polish it perfectly.
So the potter sits at his work, And turns the wheel around with his feet, Who is always focused at his work, and makes all his work by number;
He moulds the clay with his arm, and bows down his strength before his feet; He applies himself to the glazing; And he is diligent to clean the furnace.
All these rely on their hands, And everyone is skilled in his work.
Without these a city cannot be inhabited; And they could not dwell where they do, nor go up and down.

They shall not be sought in public counsel, nor sit high in the assembly; They shall not sit on the seat of judges, nor understand the ruling of judgment; They cannot declare righteousness and right- ruling; And they shall not be found where parables are spoken.
But they maintain the face of the world, And their desire is in the work of their craft.
But he who gives his mind to the Law of the Most High, And is occupied in the study of it, Seeks out of all the ancient wisdom, and is occupied in neḇuoth.
He guards the sayings of the men of name; And where wise parables are, he shall be there also.
He shall seek out the secrets of proverbs, And speak of hidden parables.
He shall serve among great men, and appear before princes; He shall travel through foreign countries; For he has examined the good and the evil among men.
He applies his heart early to look to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who made him, And shall pray before the Most High, And opens his mouth in prayer, And makes supplication for his sins.
When 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 the Almighty acts, he shall be filled with the spirit of understanding; He shall pour out wise sayings, and give thanks to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 his prayer.
He shall guide his counsel and knowledge, And on His secrets he meditates.
He reveals that which he has learned, And shall boast in the Law of the Covenant of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
Many shall commend his understanding; And as long as the world endures, it shall not be blotted out; His remembrance shall not depart, and his name shall live from generation to generation.
Nations shall speak of his wisdom, And the assembly shall declare him baruḵ.
If he dies, he shall leave a greater name than a thousand: And if he lives, he shall increase it.
Yet I have more to say, which I have thought upon; For I am filled as at the full moon.
Listen to me, you qodesh children, And bud as a rose of the field growing by the wadi;
And give a sweet fragrance as frankincense, and flourish as a lily. Send out a fragrance, and sing a song of praise, Baraḵ 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in all His works.
Exalt His Name, and extol His praise with the songs of your lips, and with harps, And in praising Him you shall say after this manner:
All the works of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 are exceedingly good, And whatever He commands shall be accomplished in due season.

And none shall say, “What is this? Why is that?” For at an appropriate time they shall all be sought out: At His command the waters stood as a heap, And the reservoir of waters at the words of His mouth.
Whatever pleases Him is done at His command; And none reverses His deliverance.
The works of all flesh are before Him, And there is none hidden from His eyes.
He sees from everlasting to everlasting; And there is no matter too marvellous for Him.
A man need not say, “What is this? Why is that?” For He has made all for their uses.
His beraḵah covered the dry land as a river, And watered it as a flood.
As He has turned the waters salty; So shall the gentiles inherit His wrath.
As His ways are clear to the qodesh; So they are stumbling blocks to the wicked.
The good matters are created for the good from the beginning; So evil matters for sinners.
The basic necessities for the whole use of man’s life are: Water, fire, iron, and salt, flour of wheat, honey, milk, and the juice of grapes, and oil, and garments.
All these are for good to the righteous; So to the sinners they are turned to evil.
There are spirits that are created for punishment, Who in their wrath lay on many strokes; In the time of destruction they pour out their strength, And appease the wrath of He who made them.
Fire, and hail, and scarcity of food, and death, All these were created for punishment;
Teeth of wild beasts, and scorpions, serpents, And the sword punishing the wicked to destruction.
They shall rejoice in His Command, and they shall be ready upon earth when needed; And when their time comes, they do not transgress His Word.
Therefore from the beginning I knew, And thought upon these, and have left them in writing.
All the works of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 are good; And He shall give all that is needed in due season;
So that a man cannot say, “This is worse than that.” For in time they all shall be prove good;
And therefore praise 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with all your heart and voice, And baraḵ the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
Great hardship is created for every man, And a heavy yoke is upon the sons of Aḏam; From the day that they go out of their mother’s womb, Till the day that they return to the mother of all.
Their imagination of what is to come, and the day of death, Are their thoughts, and fear of heart;
From he who sits on a throne of esteem, To he who is humbled in dirt and ashes;
From he who wears purple and a crown, To he who is clothed with a linen robe.
Wrath, and envy, trouble, and unrest, fear of death, and displeasure, and strife, And in the time of rest on his bed his sleep at night changes his knowledge.
He gets little or no rest, and after his sleep, is as in a day of watching, Troubled in the vision of his mind, as if he had escaped out of a battle.
When all is safe, he wakes, And marvels that the fear was naught.
These come to all flesh, both man and beast, And seven times more upon sinners.
Death, and bloodshed, strife, and sword, Calamities, scarcity of food, distress, and the scourge;
These are created for the wicked, And the flood came for their sakes.
All that are of the earth shall return to the earth again; And that which is of the waters returns to the sea.
All bribery and unrighteousness shall be blotted out; But right-dealing endures forever.
The goods of the unrighteous shall be dried up like a wadi, And shall vanish with noise, like great thunder in rain.
While the generous shall rejoice; So transgressors shall come to naught.
The children of the wicked shall not bring forth many branches; But are as unclean roots on a hard rock.
The weed growing on all water and riverbank, Shall be pulled up before any grass.
Kindness is like a most fruitful garden, And favour endures forever.
To labour, and to be content with what a man has, is a sweet life; But he who finds a treasure is above them both.
Children and the building of a city continue a man’s name; But a blameless wife is counted above them both.
Wine and music rejoice the heart; But the love of wisdom is above them both.
The flute and the harp make a sweet melody; But a pleasant tongue is above them both.
Your eye desires favour and loveliness; But more than both is grain while green.
A friend and companion never meet wrongfully; But above both is a wife with her husband.
Brothers are a help for time of trouble; But kind deeds shall deliver more than them both.
Gold and silver make a solid footing; But counsel is esteemed above them both.
Wealth and power lift the heart; But the reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is above them both. There is no lack with the reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, And with it you need not seek help.
The reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is a fruitful garden, And covers him above all esteem.
My son, do not lead a beggar’s life; For better it is to die than to beg.
The life of he who depends on another man’s table, Cannot be considered a life; For he pollutes himself with the food of other men; But a wise, disciplined man guards himself from it.
Begging is sweet in the mouth of the shameless; But in his inward parts a fire burns.

O death, how bitter is the remembrance of you to a man that lives at rest in his possessions, To the man who has no pain unto him, and that has prosperity in all; Even to he who is yet able to gain food!
O death, your lot is acceptable to the needy, And to him whose strength fails, that is now in the last age, and pained with all, And to he who despairs, and has lost patience!
Do not fear the lot of death; Remember those who have been before you, and who come after; For this is the lot from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 over all flesh.
And why are you against the decision of the Most High? There is no searching in the grave, Whether you have lived ten, or a hundred, or a thousand years.
The children of sinners are abominable children, And those who keep company in the dwelling of the wicked.
The inheritance of the children of sinners shall perish, And their descendants shall be an everlasting reproach.
The children complain of a wicked father, Because they shall be reproached for his sake.
Woe unto you, wicked men, who have forsaken the Law of the Most High Elohim! For if you increase, it shall be to your destruction:
And if you are born, you shall be born into a curse: And if you die, a curse shall be your lot.
All that are of the earth shall turn to earth again; So the wicked shall go from a curse to destruction.
The mourning of men is over their bodies; But the evil name of sinners shall be blotted out.
Have regard for your name; For that shall continue with you above a thousand great treasures of gold.
A good life has few days; But a good name endures forever.
My children, guard discipline in peace; For wisdom that is hidden, and a treasure that is not seen; What profit is there in either?
A man that hides his foolishness is better than a man that hides his wisdom.
Therefore be ashamed according to my word; For it is not good to retain all shame; Nor is it altogether approved in every matter:
Be ashamed of whoring before your father and mother; And of a lie before a prince and a mighty man;
Of an offense before a judge and ruler; Of wickedness before the assembly and people; Of unrighteous dealing before your partner and friend;
And of theft in regard to the place where you sojourn, And in regard to the truth of Elohim and His Covenant; And to lean with your elbow upon the food; And despising to give and take;
And of silence before those who greet you; And to look upon a whore;
And to turn away your face from your relative; Or to take away a portion or a gift; Or to gaze upon another man’s wife.
Or to be meddling with his female servant, And do not come near her bed; Or words of reproach before friends; And after you have given, do not reproach;
Or of repeating and speaking again that which you have heard; And of revealing of secrets.
So you shall be truly ashamed and find favour before all men.
Of these matters do not be ashamed, and allow no one to sin by them:
Of the Law of the Most High, and His Covenant; And of judgment to declare the wicked right;
Of reckoning with your partners and travellers; Or of the gift of the inheritance of friends;
Of exactness of balance and weights; Or of acquiring much or little;
And of the haughty selling by merchants; Of much correction of children; And to draw blood from the back of a wicked servant.
Where a wicked wife is, safe- keeping is good; And shut up, where many hands are.
Deliver all by number and weight; And put in writing all that you give out, or receive in.
Do not be ashamed to inform the unwise and foolish, And the very old who contends with those who are young; Thus you shall be truly learned, and approved of all men living.
The father wakes for the daughter, when no man knows; And the concern for her takes away sleep - When she is young, lest she pass the flower of youth; And being married, lest she should be hated;
In her maidenhood, lest she should be defiled and become pregnant in her father’s house; And having a husband, lest she should misbehave herself; And when she is married, lest she should be barren.
Keep a close watch over a shameless daughter, Lest she make you a laughing-stock to your enemies, And a byword in the city, and a reproach among the people, And make you ashamed before the assembly.
Do not look upon the loveliness of every woman, And do not sit in the midst of women.
For a moth comes from garments, and wickedness from women.
Better is the hardness of a man than a courteous woman, A woman who brings shame and reproach.
I shall now remember the works of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, and declare that which I have seen: In the Words of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 are His works, And all His creation does His desire.
The sun that gives light looks upon all, And its doing is full of the esteem of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has not given power to the qodeshim to declare all of His marvellous works, Which 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 the Almighty firmly settled, That whatever exists might be established for His esteem.
He seeks out the deep, and the heart, and considers their crafty schemes; For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 knows all that may be known, And He looks upon the signs of the world.
He declares matters that are past, and those to come, And reveals the path of that which is hidden.
No thought escapes Him, Nor is any word hidden from Him.
He has adorned the excellent works of His wisdom, And He is from everlasting to everlasting: Unto Him none is added, nor shall He be diminished, And He has no need of any counsellor.
Oh how desirable are all His works! And that a man may see even a spark.
All these live and remain forever for all uses, And they are all obedient.
All matters are equal, one against another; And He has made none imperfect.
One establishes the good of another; And who is ever filled with looking upon His esteem?
The pride of the heights, the clear expanse, The loveliness of the shamayim, with His esteemed display;
The sun when it appears, showing a marvellous instrument at its rising; The work of the Most High.
At noon it scorches the land, And who shall stand its burning heat?
A man blowing a furnace works with heat, But the sun burns the mountains three times more; Breathing out fiery vapours, and sending out bright rays, it blinds the eyes.
Great is 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who made it; And at His command it runs speedily.
He made the moon also to serve in its season for appointed times, And a sign for the world.
From the moon is the sign of Feasts, A light that decreases in its completion.
The new moon is called after its name, Increasing wondrously in its changing, being an instrument for the hosts above, Shining in the expanse of the shamayim;
The loveliness of the shamayim, the esteem of the stars, An ornament giving light in the highest places of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
At the command of the Qadosh One they stand in their order, And never weary in their watches.
Look upon the rainbow, and praise He who made it; It is very lovely in its brightness.
It surrounds the shamayim with a splendid arc, And the hands of the Most High have bent it.
By His command He makes the snow to fall in place, And sends the lightnings of His judgment swiftly.
Through this the storehouses are opened; And clouds fly onward as birds.
By His great power He makes the clouds pour out, And the hailstones are broken small.
At His sight the mountains are shaken, And at His desire the south wind blows.
The noise of thunder causes the earth to tremble; So does the northern storm and the whirlwind. As birds flying He scatters the snow, And its falling is as the settling of grasshoppers.
The eye marvels at the loveliness of its whiteness, And the heart is astonished at its falling.
He also pours the frost as salt upon the earth, And being hardened, it lays on the top as sharp icicles.
When the cold north wind blows, and the water is hardened into ice, It remains upon every collection of water, And clothes the water like a breastplate.
It devours the mountains, and burns the wilderness, And consumes the grass like fire.
A mist coming speedily stands as a healer of all, A refreshing dew coming after heat.
By His counsel He calms the deep, And plants islands within it.
Those who sail on the sea tell of its dangers; And when we hear it with our ears, we marvel at it.
For in it are strange and wondrous works, Differing kinds of all creatures and whales created.
By Him the end of them has a benefit of good, And by His word all exists.
We may speak much, and yet come short; Therefore in summary, He is all.
How are we able to exalt Him? For He is great above all His works.
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 is awesome and exceedingly great, And His power is marvellous.
When you esteem 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, exalt Him as much as you may; For He shall even yet far exceed. And when you exalt Him, deliver all your strength, And do not be weary; for you shall never declare enough.
Who has seen Him, that he might tell us? And who could exalt Him as He is?
There are still greater than these which are hidden, For we have seen but a few of His works.
For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has made all; And to the reverent has he given wisdom.
Let us now baraḵ men of name, And our fathers who brought us forth.
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 has worked great esteem by them, Through His great power from the beginning.
Those who ruled in their reigns, men named for their strength, Giving counsel by their understanding, and declaring neḇuoth.
Leaders of the people by their counsels; And by their knowledge of learning, fitting for the people, Wise and learned are their instructions.
Such who compose musical songs, and speak verses in writing;
Wealthy men equipped with resource, living peaceably in their dwellings;
All these were esteemed in their generations, And were the esteem of their times.
There are some of them who have left behind a name, That their bireḵoth might be declared.
And there are some who have no remembrance; Who have perished as though they had never been; And have become as though they had never been born; And their children after them.
But these were kind men, Whose righteousness has not been forgotten.
With their seed a good inheritance shall continually remain, And their children are within the Covenant.
Their seed stands fast, And their children for their sakes.
Their seed shall remain forever, And their esteem shall not be blotted out.
Their bodies are buried in peace; But their name lives forever.
The people shall tell of their wisdom, And the assembly shall declare their praise.
Ḥanoḵ pleased 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and was translated, Being an example of repentance to all generations.
Noaḥ was found perfect and righteous; In the time of wrath he was taken in exchange; Therefore he was left as a remnant upon the earth when the flood came.
An everlasting Covenant was made with him, That no longer would all flesh perish by the flood.
Aḇraham was a great father of many people; There was none like him in esteem;
Who kept the Law of the Most High, and was in Covenant with Him. He established the Covenant in his flesh; And when he was tried, he was found trustworthy.

Therefore He assured him with an oath, That He would baraḵ the nations in his seed, And that He would multiply him as the dust of the earth, And exalt his seed as the stars, and cause them to inherit from sea to sea, And from the River unto the utmost part of the land.

With Yitsḥaq He likewise established the beraḵah of all men, and the Covenant, And caused it to rest upon the head of Ya’aqoḇ. He acknowledged him with His beraḵah, And gave him an inheritance, and divided his portions; Among the twelve tribes He divided them.
And He brought out from him a kind man, who found favour in the sight of all flesh, Even Mosheh, beloved of Elohim and men, whose remembrance is baruḵ.
He made him like the esteemed qodeshim, And exalted him, so that his enemies stood in fear of him.
By his words He caused the wonders to cease, And He made him esteemed in the sight of sovereigns, And gave him a Command for His people, And showed him part of His esteem.
He qadosh him in his trustworthiness and humility, And chose him out of all men.

He caused him to hear His voice, and brought him into the thick cloud, And gave him Commands before His face, Even the Law of Ḥai and knowledge, That he might teach Ya’aqoḇ His Covenant, And Yisra’ĕl his Right-Rulings.
He exalted Aharon, a qodesh man like him, Even his brother, of the tribe of Lĕwi.
He made an everlasting Covenant with him, And gave him the kehunnah among the people; He adorned him with comely ornaments, And clothed him with a robe of esteem.
He put upon him perfect esteem; And strengthened him with splendid garments, With linen trousers, with a long robe, and the shoulder garment.

And He surrounded it with pomegranates, And with many golden bells all around, So that as he walked there would be a sound, And a noise made that would be heard in the Hĕyḵal, For a remembrance to the children of His people;
With a qodesh garment of gold and blue silk and purple, The work of embroidery with a breastplate of Right- Ruling, And with Urim and Tummim;

With woven scarlet, the work of the skilled workman, With precious stones engraved like seals, and mounted in gold, The work of the engraver with writing engraved for a remembrance, After the number of the tribes of Yisra’ĕl.
He placed a crown of gold upon the turban, in which was engraved QODESHAH, An ornament of esteem, a precious work, The desire of the eyes, elegant and lovely.
Before him there were none like them, Nor did any stranger ever put them on, But only his children and his children’s children for all time.
Their offerings shall be completely consumed twice every day continually.

Mosheh ordained him, and anointed him with qodesh oil: This was appointed to him with an everlasting Covenant, And to his seed, so long as the shamayim should remain, That they should serve Him, and execute the office of the kehunnah, And baraḵ the people in His Name.
He chose him out of all men living to offer slaughterings to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, Incense, and a sweet savour, for a remembrance, To make atonement for His people.
He gave him His Commands, and authority in the Laws of Right-Rulings, That he should teach Ya’aqoḇ the Witnesses, And instruct Yisra’ĕl in His Torot.
Foreigners conspired together against him, And scorned him in the wilderness, Even the men that were on the side of Dathan and Aḇiram, And the assembly of Qoraḥ, with rage and wrath.
This 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 saw, and it displeased Him, And in His wrathful displeasure they were consumed; He did wonders upon them, to consume them with the fiery flame.
But he made Aharon more esteemed, And gave him an inheritance, and divided to him the first-fruits of the increase; Most of all He prepared bread in abundance;
For they eat of the offerings of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, Which He gave to him and his seed.
However in the land of the people he had no inheritance, Nor had he any portion among the people; For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Himself is his portion and inheritance.

The third in esteem is Pineḥas the son of Eli’ezer, Because he had ardour in the reverence of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, And stood up with good courage of heart when the people were turned back, And made atonement for Yisra’ĕl.
Therefore there was a Covenant of peace made with him, That he should be the chief of the Miqdash and of His people, And that he and his descendants should have the height of the kehunnah forever;

According to the Covenant made with Dawiḏ son of Yishai, of the tribe of Yahuḏah, That the inheritance of the sovereign should be to his descendants alone; So the inheritance of Aharon should also be to his seed.
Elohim give you wisdom in your heart to rightly- rule His people in righteousness, That their good is not abolished, and that their esteem may endure forever.

Yahoshua the son a Nun was a brave warrior, And was the successor of Mosheh in neḇuoth, Who according to his name was made great for the saving of the elect of Elohim, And taking vengeance on the enemies that rose up against them, That he might place Yisra’ĕl in their inheritance.
What great esteem he attained, when he lifted up his hands, And stretched out his sword against the cities!
Who before him ever stood up to it? For 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Himself brought his enemies to him.
Did the sun not go back by His doing? And was not one day as long as two?
He called upon the Most High Ĕl, when the enemies pressed upon him on every side; And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 the Almighty heard him.

And with hailstones of great strength He made the battle fall violently against the nations, And at the descent he destroyed those who resisted, That the nations might know all their strength, Because he fought in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, And he followed the Almighty.
In the time of Mosheh he also did a work of kindness, He and Kalĕḇ the son of Yephunneh, In that they withstood the assembly, And withheld the people from sin, and appeased the wicked murmuring.
And of six hundred thousand people on foot, These two were preserved to bring them into the inheritance, Even to the land that flows with milk and honey.
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 also gave strength to Kalĕḇ, Who remained with him to his old age; So that he entered into the high places of the land, And his seed obtained it for an inheritance;
That all the children of Yisra’ĕl might see that it is good to follow 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
And concerning the judges, every one by name, Whose heart did not go whoring, nor departed from 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, Let their memory be baruḵ.
Let their bones flourish from their place, And let the name of those who were esteemed be continued upon their children.
Shemu’ĕl, the naḇi of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, beloved of his Aḏon, Established a reign, and anointed princes over His people.
By the Law of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 he rightly-ruled the assembly, And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 showed respect toward Ya’aqoḇ.
By his trustworthiness he was found a true naḇi, And by his word he was known to be trustworthy in vision.
He called upon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 the Almighty, When his enemies pressed upon him on every side, When he offered the suckling lamb.
And 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 thundered from the shamayim, And with a great noise made His voice heard.
And He destroyed the rulers of the Tsorites, And all the princes of the Pelishtites.
And before his long sleep he bore witness in the sight of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 and His anointed, “I have not taken any man’s goods, so much as a shoe.” And no man accused him.
And after his death he naḇa, and showed the sovereign his end, And lifted up his voice from the earth in neḇuah, To blot out the wickedness of the people.
And after him rose up Nathan to naḇa in the time of Dawiḏ.
As the fat is taken away from the peace offering, So Dawiḏ was chosen out of the children of Yisra’ĕl.
He played with lions as with young goats, And bears as with lambs.
Did he not slay a giant, when he was still young? And did he not take away the reproach of the people, When he lifted up his hand with the stone in the sling, And beat down the boasting of Golyath?
For he called upon the Most High Ĕl; And He gave him strength in his right hand to slay that mighty warrior, And raise up the horn of His people.
So the people esteemed him with ten thousands, And praised him with the bireḵoth of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, In that He gave him a crown of esteem.
For he destroyed their enemies on every side, And brought to naught his adversaries, the Pelishtites, And broke their horn in pieces to this day.
In all his works he praised the Qadosh One Most High with words of esteem; With his whole heart he sang songs, And loved He who made him.
He also appointed singers before the altar, That with their voices they made sweet melody, And sang praises daily with their songs.
He adorned their Feasts, and put in order the Appointed Times until the end, That they should praise His qodesh Name, And that the Hĕyḵal might resound from the morning.
𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 took away his sins, and exalted his horn forever: He gave him a Covenant of sovereigns, And a throne of esteem in Yisra’ĕl.
After him rose up a wise son, and for his sake his dwelling was broad.
Shelomoh reigned in a peaceable time, and was esteemed; For Elohim made quiet all around him, That he might build a House for His Name, And prepare His Miqdash forever.
How wise you were in your youth, And filled with understanding as a flood!
Your being covered the whole earth, and you filled it with deep parables.
Your name went to the far islands; And for your peace you were loved.
The lands marvelled at you for your songs, and proverbs, and parables, and interpretations.
By the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim, which is called 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Elohim of Yisra’ĕl, You gathered gold as tin and multiplied silver as lead.
You bowed your loins to women, And by your body you were brought into subjection.
You stained your esteem, and polluted your seed; So that you brought wrath upon your children, And were grieved for your folly.
So the reign was divided, and out of Ephrayim ruled a rebellious reign.

But the kindness of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 shall never cease, Nor shall any of His works perish, Neither shall He cut off the descendants of His elect, And the seed of he who loves Him He shall not take away; Therefore He gave a remnant to Ya’aqoḇ, And out of him, a root of Dawiḏ.

Thus Shelomoh rested with his fathers, And of his seed he left behind him Reḥaḇ’am, Even the foolishness of the people, and one who had no understanding, Who turned the people away through his counsel. There was also Yaroḇ’am the son of Neḇat, Who caused Yisra’ĕl to sin, and showed Ephrayim the way of sin;
And their sins were multiplied exceedingly, So they were driven out of the land.
For they sought out all wickedness, Till the punishment came upon them.
Then Ĕliyahu the naḇi stood up as fire, And his word burned like a lamp.
He brought a severe scarcity of food upon them, And by his ardour he diminished their number.
By the word of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 he shut up the shamayim, And also brought down fire three times.
O Ĕliyahu, how you were esteemed in your wondrous deeds! And whose esteem is like yours?
Who raised up a dead man from death, And his being from the place of the dead, By the word of the Most High;
Who brought sovereigns to destruction, And honourable men from their bed;
Who heard the rebuke of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 at Sinai, And the judgment of punishment in Ḥorĕḇ;
Who anointed sovereigns to take vengeance, And neḇi’im to succeed after him;
Who was taken up in a whirlwind of fire, And in a chariot of fiery horses;

Who were ordained for reproofs in their times, To appease the wrath of judgment of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, Before it broke forth into wrath, And to turn the heart of the father to the son, And to restore the tribes of Ya’aqoḇ.
Baruḵ are those who saw You, and slept in love; For we shall surely live.
It was Ĕliyahu who was covered with a whirlwind; And Ĕlisha was filled with His Ruaḥ. While he lived, he was not moved by the presence of any prince, Nor could any bring him into subjection.
No word could overcome him; And after his death his being naḇa.
He did wonders in his life, And at his death his works were marvellous.

For all this the people did not repent, Nor did they depart from their sins, Till they were plundered and carried out of their land, And were scattered through all the earth; Yet there remained a remnant of the people, And a ruler from the house of Dawiḏ;
Of whom some did that which was pleasing to Elohim, And some multiplied sins.
Ḥizqiyahu fortified his city, and brought in water into the midst of it; He dug the solid rock with tools of iron, And made wells for water.
In his time Sanḥĕriḇ came up, and sent the Raḇshaqĕh, And lifted up his hand against Tsiyon, And boasted proudly.
Then their hearts and hands trembled, And they were in pain, as women in childbirth.
But they called upon 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 who is kind, And stretched out their hands toward Him. And immediately the Qadosh One heard them out of the shamayim, And delivered them by the service of Yeshayahu.
He smote the army of Ashshur, And His messenger destroyed them.
For Ḥizqiyahu had done that which pleased 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, And was strong in the Ways of Dawiḏ his father, As Yeshayahu the naḇi, who was great and trustworthy in his vision, had commanded him.
In his time the sun went backward, And he lengthened the sovereign’s life.
He saw by an excellent spirit what would come to pass, And he comforted those who mourned in Tsiyon.
He showed what should come to be at the end of time, And secrets before they came to be.
The remembrance of Yoshiyahu is like the composition of a perfume that is made with the skill of the perfumer; It is sweet as honey in all mouths, And as music at a feast of wine.
He acted uprightly by instructing the people, And took away the wicked abominations.
He directed his heart toward 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, And in the time of the wicked he established the worship of Elohim.
All except Dawiḏ and Ḥizqiyahu and Yoshiyahu, were wicked; For they forsook the Law of the Most High, Even the sovereigns of Yahuḏah failed.
Therefore He gave their strength to others, And their esteem to a foreign nation.
They burned the chosen city of the Miqdash, And made the streets desolate, According to the neḇuah of Yirmeyahu.
For they treated him evilly, who was yet a naḇi, qadosh in his mother’s womb, That he might root out, and afflict, and destroy; And that he might also build up, and plant.
It was Yeḥezqĕl who saw the esteemed vision, Which was shown to him upon the chariot of the keruḇim.
For he remembered the enemies under the sign of rain, And directed those who went rightly.
And of the twelve neḇi’im let their remembrance be baruḵ, And let their bones flourish again out of their place; For they comforted Ya’aqoḇ, and delivered them with true expectancy.
How shall we exalt Zerubbaḇel? Even he was as a signet on the right hand;
So was Yĕshua son of Yotsaḏaq; Who in their time built the House, And raised a qodesh Hĕyḵal to 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, Which was prepared for everlasting esteem.
And among the elect was Neḥemyah, Whose name is great, who raised up for us the walls that had fallen, And put up the gates and the bars, and raised up our ruins again.
But no man on the earth was created like Ḥanoḵ; For he was taken from the earth.
Neither was there a young man born like Yosĕph, A governor over his brothers, a support to the people, Whose bones were regarded by 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄.
Shĕm and Shĕth were in great esteem among men, And so was Aḏam above every living creature in creation.
Shim’on the kohĕn ha’gadol, the son of Onyah, Who in his life repaired the House again, And in his days fortified the Hĕyḵal;
And by him the double height from the foundation was built, The high fortress of the wall around the Hĕyḵal;
In his days the cistern to receive water, being surrounded as the sea, Was covered with plates of bronze;
He looked after of the Hĕyḵal that it should not fall, And fortified the city against a siege.
How esteemed he was in the midst of the people, When coming out of the Miqdash!
He was as the morning star in the midst of a cloud, And as the moon in its fullness;
As the sun shining upon the Hĕyḵal of the Most High, And as the rainbow giving light in the bright clouds,
And as the flower of roses in the spring of the year; As lilies by the rivers of water, And as the branches of frankincense in the time of summer;
As fire and incense in the fire holder, And as a vessel of beaten gold mounted with all kinds of precious stones;
And as a fair olive tree budding forth fruit, And as a cypress which grows up to the clouds.
When he put on the robe of esteem, And was clothed with the perfection of esteem, When he went up to the qodesh altar, He made the garment of qodeshah esteemed.
When he took the portion out of the hands of the kohenim, He himself stood by the hearth of the altar, Surrounded as a young cedar in Leḇanon; And as palm trees they surrounded him.
So were all the sons of Aharon in their esteem, And the offerings of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 in their hands, Before all the assembly of Yisra’ĕl.
And finishing the service at the altar, That he might adorn the offering of the Most High Almighty,
He stretched out his hand to the cup, And pouring the blood of the grape, He poured out at the foot of the altar, A sweet fragrance to the Most High Sovereign of all.
Then the sons of Aharon shouted, And sounded the silver trumpets, And made a great noise to be heard, For a remembrance before the Most High.
Then all the people hurried together, And fell down on their faces on the earth to worship 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 Ĕl Shaddai, the Most High.
The singers also sang praises with their voices, With all kinds of sounds sweet melody was made.
And the people sought 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 the Most High, By prayer before He who is kind, Till the qodeshah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 had ended, And they had finished His service.
Then he went down, and raised his hands over the whole assembly of the children of Yisra’ĕl, To give the beraḵah of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 with his lips, and to rejoice in His Name.
And they bowed themselves down to worship a second time, That they might receive a beraḵah from the Most High.
Now therefore baraḵ the Elohim of all, Who does only wondrously everywhere, Who exalts our days from the womb, And deals with us according to His kindness.
He gives joy to the heart, And that peace may be in our days in Yisra’ĕl forever;
That He would confirm His kindness with us, And deliver us in His time!
There are two manner of nations which my heart abhors, And the third is no nation:
Those who sit on the mountain of Shomeron, And those who dwell among the Pelishtites, And those foolish people who dwell in Sheḵem.
Yahoshua the son of Sira of Yerushalayim, Has written in this book the instruction of understanding and knowledge, From whose heart poured out wisdom.
Baruḵ is he who shall be exercised in these; And he who treasures them up in his heart shall become wise.
For if he does them, he shall be strong in all; For the light of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 leads he who gives wisdom to the reverent. Baruḵ be the Name of 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄 forever. Amĕn, Amĕn.
A Prayer of Yahoshua the son of Sira.
I thank you, O Aḏon and Sovereign, And praise You, O Elohim my Saviour; I give praise to Your Name;

For You are my Defender and Helper, And have preserved my body from destruction, And from the snare of the slanderous tongue, And from the lips that forge lies, And have been my Helper against my adversaries;

And have delivered me, according to the multitude of Your kindnesses and greatness of Your Name, From the teeth of those who were ready to devour me, And out of the hands of those who sought after my life, And from the great afflictions which I had;
From the choking fire on every side, And from the midst of the fire which I did not kindle;
From the depth of the inward parts of She’ol, From an unclean tongue, and from lying words.
By an accusation to the sovereign from an unrighteous tongue, My being drew near unto death, My life was near to She’ol beneath.
They surrounded me on every side, And there was no one to help me. I looked for the support of men, but there was none.
Then I thought upon Your favour, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, And upon Your acts of old, How You save those who wait on You, And save them out of the hands of their enemies.
Then I lifted up my supplications from the earth, And prayed for deliverance from death,
I called upon Aḏonai 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄, the Father, That He would not leave me in the days of my trouble, And in the time of the proud, when there was no help.
I praise Your Name continually, And sing praises with thanksgiving; And so my prayer is heard.
For You saved me from destruction, And delivered me from the evil time; Therefore I thank and praise You, And baraḵ Your Name, O 𐤉𐤄𐤅𐤄!
